name: The Academy, year two
cadence: weekdays, one lesson per weekday; thirteen blocks of twenty lessons, one subject for four weeks of weekdays straight
target_length: 60–120 minutes of reading (13,000–26,000 words), working target 75–90 minutes, written in four to six parts
note: Logan's direction of 2026-09-11: thirteen topics, twenty lessons each, far deeper and more advanced than the 150-day year, up to one to two hours a day, covering a full year. Blocks run in file order after year one's day 150 (projected 2027-03-12). The Finance & Markets, Accounting and Wealth Management courses are shaped on the public CFA, CPA and CFP bodies of knowledge with no claim of affiliation. Block 9 (AI, Technology & Coding) is re-planned from current sources on its first morning (refresh_before_run). No quizzes, no problem sets, no self-assessment. Procedure: prompts/learning.md → Year Two.
order_decisions: Logan's block order is kept as given (Physics runs before Mathematics; the physics lessons therefore carry the geometry and group theory they need rather than assuming block 6). Inside Economics, the micro half runs before the macro half because the macro lessons build on consumer duality and industrial organisation.

blocks.title: Finance & Markets I: Statements, Capital and the Value of Equity
blocks.subject: Finance & Markets
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that turn year one's finance vocabulary into an analyst's working method: the statistical tests investors actually run, the financial statements read at the depth a professional reads them and adjusted where they mislead, the corporate decisions on capital, leverage, payout and deals judged against theory and evidence, and four independent routes to the value of a share — every one built on real 10-K figures and live market prices. By the end, a filing and a price are enough to produce and defend a valuation.
blocks.modelled_on: The public CFA Program topic areas at Levels I and II — Quantitative Methods, Financial Statement Analysis, Corporate Issuers and Equity Investments — in the order the CFA Institute Investment Series texts teach them (Quantitative Investment Analysis; International Financial Statement Analysis; Corporate Finance; Equity Asset Valuation), cross-checked against Brealey–Myers–Allen, Damodaran and Penman. No affiliation with CFA Institute is claimed or implied.
blocks.capstone: Take any US-listed company's latest 10-K and market price and produce a defensible valuation range by four independent methods — dividend discount, FCFF/FCFE, residual income and justified multiples — on statements adjusted for revenue quality, leases, pensions, deferred taxes and intercorporate holdings, with a cost of capital built bottom-up and the company's capital-allocation, leverage, payout and M&A choices judged on theory and evidence; then carry the same discipline to a company with no quoted price.

blocks.title: Finance & Markets II: From the Curve to the Trade
blocks.subject: Finance & Markets
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that take the reader from the Treasury curve to a finished, honestly tested systematic strategy: fixed income and credit at desk depth, derivatives priced and hedged beyond Black–Scholes, the alternatives with their fees, their leverage and the LBO model exposed, and Level-III-depth portfolio management — allocation, factors, risk, attribution, the investor's constraints and the profession's standards of conduct — before the block ends on how a trade actually happens and how a backtest lies. Every lesson runs on real instruments at their run-date prices, and every number says where it came from.
blocks.modelled_on: The public CFA Program curriculum topic areas (Level II Fixed Income, Derivatives and Alternative Investments; Level III Asset Allocation, Portfolio Construction, Performance Measurement, Derivatives and Risk Management, Ethical and Professional Standards, and the Portfolio Management and Private Wealth pathways), with the rates and options chapters shaped after Tuckman & Serrat's Fixed Income Securities and Gatheral's The Volatility Surface, and the trading chapters after Harris's Trading and Exchanges and López de Prado's Advances in Financial Machine Learning — with no claim of affiliation with any of them.
blocks.capstone: The reader can take a live market — the Treasury curve, a corporate bond and its CDS, an option chain, a fund's cash flows — and price, hedge, allocate, attribute and execute against it at the standard of a professional desk; and can build a systematic strategy end to end, fit a regime model to it, and judge its backtest with the deflated Sharpe ratio, purged cross-validation and cost realism, writing a research note that survives a sceptical reader.

blocks.title: Advanced Micro & Macro Economics
blocks.subject: Economics
blocks.mission: Ten graduate-level micro lessons take the discipline to the bottom first: duality, general equilibrium, games, information, mechanisms, causal inference, industrial organization, behaviour, taxation and market design, worked on real antitrust cases, real auctions and real experiments — and, in passing, the consumer's problem, the monopolistic price-setter and the identification toolkit that the macro half then assumes rather than re-derives. Ten macro lessons then rebuild the models that sit behind every FOMC statement, CBO outlook, JOLTS release and recession call — growth, consumption and investment, the New Keynesian core, policy rules, debt dynamics, the open economy, search unemployment, financial frictions, expectations and nowcasting — each solved on FRED and BLS data rather than on a blackboard. Together they leave the reader able to name the model a headline is silently assuming and to check it against the data the same morning.
blocks.modelled_on: A first-year graduate sequence in economics: for the micro half, Mas-Colell, Whinston and Green's Microeconomic Theory, Tirole's Theory of Industrial Organization, Krishna's Auction Theory and Angrist–Pischke's Mostly Harmless Econometrics; for the macro half, Romer's Advanced Macroeconomics (5th ed.), Galí's Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle (2nd ed.) and Obstfeld–Rogoff's Foundations of International Macroeconomics — with the 2023 DOJ/FTC Merger Guidelines, the NRMP's published match data, the Federal Reserve's Monetary Policy Report and the CBO's Long-Term Budget Outlook as the working documents. No affiliation with any institution or body.
blocks.capstone: By day 20 Logan can take the morning's release or ruling — a merger complaint, a Treasury auction result, a Match Day announcement, an FOMC statement, a JOLTS print, a CBO projection — and reconstruct the model behind it with numbers: price an Arrow security, derive an equilibrium bid, calculate a merger's HHI and upward pricing pressure, read a difference-in-differences table for its parallel-trends claim, run deferred acceptance by hand, solve the three-equation New Keynesian model, run the r–g arithmetic on the current debt path and compute u* from the vacancy rate — and say which of the twenty models the headline silently assumes and where that model is known to fail.

blocks.title: Advanced Physics: the Mathematics Done
blocks.subject: Physics
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that take year one's 26 physics days from statement to derivation: the variational and Hamiltonian machinery of mechanics, Maxwell with potentials and radiation, relativity in four-vector and tensor form, quantum mechanics from Hilbert space to scattering, statistical mechanics from the partition function to the quantum gases, and the fields that come after — condensed matter, nuclei and particles, quantum fields, plasmas, Hamiltonian chaos and the observed universe. Every lesson does the mathematics rather than gesturing at it, and every lesson lands on a real orbit, a real transition frequency or a real detector result. Because Physics runs before the Mathematics block, no lesson assumes anything from it: where a lesson needs tensor calculus (day 8), the rotation group (day 11), the spectral theorem (day 10) or a Green's function (days 6 and 13), it carries that mathematics as a part of its own, built on year one.
blocks.modelled_on: The standard upper-undergraduate and first-year-graduate physics sequence as codified in Goldstein (Classical Mechanics), Jackson and Griffiths (Electrodynamics), Carroll and Hartle (General Relativity), Sakurai and Griffiths (Quantum Mechanics), Pathria and Kardar (Statistical Mechanics), Ashcroft & Mermin and Kittel (Solid State), Peskin & Schroeder (QFT), Chen (Plasma Physics), Lichtenberg & Lieberman (Hamiltonian Chaos) and Ryden/Dodelson (Cosmology), with no claim of affiliation to any institution
blocks.capstone: Compute the age and composition of the universe from the Planck 2018 parameters, read a CMB power spectrum and a BAO distance ladder, and state exactly what the Hubble tension and the DESI dark-energy result do and do not show — with the Friedmann equations, the thermal history and the statistical-mechanical distributions behind them derived rather than quoted.

blocks.title: Philosophy: How We Know, How We Should Live
blocks.subject: Philosophy
blocks.mission: Ten lessons on how we know — logic and its limits, justification and scepticism, induction and probability, science, language, metaphysics, mathematics, mind, the self and free will, and rational choice — followed by ten on how we should live: metaethics, the three great normative theories and contractualism, character and meaning, God, the state, law, markets, machines, and the risks we impose on people not yet born. Every lesson sets the primary texts against each other and settles what can be settled by formalising the argument, running the thought experiment to its end, or doing the decision-theoretic sum with real numbers; none is a survey, and none re-teaches year one. The reader finishes able to state a philosophical position precisely, find the premise that carries it, and say what it would cost to give it up.
blocks.modelled_on: The reading lists of a graduate-level analytic-philosophy survey: the core entries of the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy; the standard anthologies (Chalmers, Philosophy of Mind: Classical and Contemporary Readings; Benacerraf & Putnam, Philosophy of Mathematics; Shafer-Landau, Ethical Theory; Goodin & Pettit, Contemporary Political Philosophy); and the primary texts in their standard scholarly editions (Hackett, Cambridge Texts in the History of Philosophy, Oxford World's Classics, the Clarendon Hume and Locke). No claim of affiliation with any institution.
blocks.capstone: Take a real decision that imposes risk on other people — a discount rate for a climate policy, a threshold for a classifier, a bet on a far-future payoff — and carry it through expected utility, the Ramsey rule with Stern's and Nordhaus's parameters, Parfit's non-identity problem and the fanaticism objection, stating at each step which premise is doing the work, which normative theory from the second half it presupposes, and what the reader would have to believe about knowledge and persons from the first half for the answer to stand.

blocks.title: Advanced Mathematics: Analysis, Chance, Computation and Structure
blocks.subject: Mathematics
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that take the mathematics year one taught as tools and rebuild it as a discipline: analysis and measure first, so that probability, martingales and stochastic calculus can be proved rather than asserted; the equations of change (ODE and dynamical systems, PDE, complex, Fourier) next; then optimisation, computation and inference at the level a quant or a scientist actually works at; and finally the structures — groups, computation and its limits, graphs, manifolds — that the rest of the year and the newspaper keep meeting. Because the Physics block has already run, the dynamical-systems, geometry and group-theory lessons are taught as mathematics in their own right — the theorems beneath the phenomena Physics showed — rather than as a toolkit for relativity or quantum mechanics; and because Finance day 3 has already fitted the classical time-series models, the time-series lesson is the state-space and Kalman theory that owns them. Every lesson proves something and computes something with real, dated numbers, and every one is chosen both for what a later block needs and for its own beauty.
blocks.modelled_on: The first-year graduate core of a mathematics department (real analysis, measure-theoretic probability, ODE/PDE, complex analysis, numerical analysis) combined with the stochastic-calculus and statistics sequence of a financial-mathematics master's programme, shaped on the canonical texts — Rudin, Folland, Williams, Strogatz, Evans, Ahlfors, Stein & Shakarchi, Shreve, Boyd & Vandenberghe, Casella & Berger, Gelman et al., Cover & Thomas, Durbin & Koopman, Dummit & Foote, Sipser, Katz & Lindell, Newman, Spivak, do Carmo and Lee — with no claim of affiliation with any institution.
blocks.capstone: By day 20 the reader can verify Gauss–Bonnet on a surface he can hold — sixty corners of twelve degrees adding to 720° on the football and on C₆₀ — integrate a form over a manifold and apply Stokes' theorem in any dimension, compute Christoffel symbols and curvature from a metric and predict how far a Foucault pendulum turns in a day; and, across the block, can prove the strong law and the central limit theorem, construct Brownian motion and Itô's lemma, rewrite Black–Scholes as the heat equation, prove a limit cycle exists and compute the normal form of a bifurcation, solve a convex programme through its dual, control numerical error and report a computed number honestly, fit and test a likelihood, run and diagnose an MCMC sampler, code a message near its entropy, put any classical series model in state-space form and run its Kalman filter as Bayes' rule, prove a problem undecidable or NP-complete, and read RSA, the TLS handshake, secp256k1 and PageRank as arithmetic on groups and graphs.

blocks.title: Political Science and Its Theories
blocks.subject: Political Science
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that run from the origins of the state to the designs political scientists found in the wild: how power is organized, contested, delegated and lost, in the United States and in comparison, and what the evidence — real roll-call votes, certified election returns, sanctions episodes with numbers — actually shows. Every theory is attributed to its holders and set beside its strongest rival, in the newspaper's neutral sense; the block ends with the discipline's own designs — close elections, redistricting and lotteries, survey and conjoint experiments — and its replication record, taking the econometric toolkit as taught in the Economics block, so the reader can read a political-science paper and judge whether its causal claim survives.
blocks.modelled_on: The public structure of a graduate first-year sequence in political science — comparative politics, American institutions, political behaviour, political economy and formal theory, international relations, and research design — shaped after the canonical texts in each field (Weber, Tilly, Olson, Dahl, Przeworski, Duverger, Cox, Krehbiel, Neustadt, Segal–Spaeth, Zaller, Downs, Fearon, Waltz, Keohane, Svolik, Skocpol, Dunning, Gerber–Green) and the standard peer-reviewed papers; no affiliation with any department, association or credentialing body is claimed.
blocks.capstone: Take any empirical political-science paper — a close-election regression discontinuity, a redistricting or lottery natural experiment, a conjoint or field experiment — identify its design, state its identifying assumption in one sentence, say what would break it, check the result against its pre-registration and the replication record, and judge whether the causal claim survives; and, on the way there, decompose a certified election result into turnout and persuasion, count the veto players on a bill, size a sanctions episode against its forecast, and place a theory beside its strongest rival without taking a side.

blocks.title: Rocketry: Propulsion, Flight and Return
blocks.subject: Rocketry
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that take the launch vehicle apart at the level of a graduate propulsion and astrodynamics sequence: the nozzle and the chemistry first, then the engine cycles, pumps, injectors, cooling and solid motors that year one only named; then the vehicle — tanks, structures, navigation, control, the optimal ascent and the optimal staging; then the orbit, the planets and the way back down; and finally what reuse, range safety and the slow electric and nuclear engines cost and buy. Every lesson runs its arithmetic on real hardware — Merlin, Raptor, RL10, BE-4, Rutherford, P120C and GEM-63XL, Falcon 9, Starship, Electron, Vulcan, New Glenn and Ariane 6 — so that by the end the reader can size, fly and price a launch vehicle from the injector face to the landing burn.
blocks.modelled_on: A graduate propulsion and astrodynamics sequence, shaped after Sutton & Biblarz's Rocket Propulsion Elements (9th ed.), Huzel & Huang's Modern Engineering for Design of Liquid-Propellant Rocket Engines (AIAA, 1992), Curtis's Orbital Mechanics for Engineering Students (4th ed.), Vallado's Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications (4th ed.) and the NASA SP-8000 space vehicle design criteria monographs — with no claim of affiliation with any institution.
blocks.capstone: By the last lesson the reader can size an electric-propulsion or nuclear-thermal stage from the power–thrust–Isp triangle, fly it on a low-thrust trajectory, and set it beside the chemical vehicle assembled over the previous nineteen lessons — nozzle, chamber, cycle, pumps, injector, cooling, tanks, structure, navigation, control, ascent, staging, perturbed orbit, rendezvous, interplanetary transfer, entry, landing, reuse and range — with every number on the comparison traceable to a real engine, a real mission, a real standard or a real filing.

blocks.title: Models, Machines and the Code Between
blocks.subject: AI, Technology & Coding
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that take the transformer apart to the attention head and the routing gate, put it on the machine it runs on, follow it through a training run, a serving stack, post-training and evaluation, and then step back to the engineering disciplines — systems, data work, automation, security — that Logan's own newspaper depends on, ending with what language models have actually found in the text that markets read. This is a fixed spine of twenty slots whose titles, order and prerequisites hold; because the block runs about a year after it was written, the routine re-plans the specifics of every slot from current primary sources on the block's first morning (prompts/learning.md §Y4, writing state/learning-refresh.json), keeping each spine title whose content still holds and replacing what the field has superseded.
blocks.modelled_on: The public syllabi of graduate language-model-systems courses (Stanford CS336 Language Modeling from Scratch and CS224N, CMU 11-711), the canonical papers each lesson names and the labs' own technical reports and system cards; for the engineering half, Kleppmann's Designing Data-Intensive Applications, McKinney's Python for Data Analysis, the OWASP Top 10 and NIST AI 100-2 catalogues, and López de Prado's Advances in Financial Machine Learning — with no claim of affiliation with any of them.
blocks.capstone: By day 20 the reader can take a published claim that a model, a dataset or a text signal does something — a benchmark score, a serving cost per token, a filing that predicts returns, an agent that 'handles' a workflow — and reconstruct from first principles what would have to be true for the claim to hold: the FLOPs and bytes, the acceptance rates and error bars, the trust boundaries, the look-ahead a text corpus hides and the point-in-time data; and can design, code, test, version and secure a small quantitative pipeline of his own, including the one that writes this newspaper.

blocks.title: FAR at Depth: The Codification Applied
blocks.subject: Accounting
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that take the financial-reporting body of knowledge — the framework, revenue, inventory, fair value and investments, plant, intangibles, leases, taxes, pensions, share-based pay, equity and EPS, combinations, consolidation, currency, cash flows, the notes, and the not-for-profit and governmental frameworks — to the level at which every standard is cited by number and applied to a named filing with journal entries carried through the statements. Where year one taught what a balance sheet says, this block teaches how each line was measured and what choice sat behind the measurement. Block 2 (Accounting II) then turns to audit, tax and the analysis that sits on top of the numbers.
blocks.modelled_on: The public AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints — the FAR core section (Area I Financial Reporting, Area II Select Balance Sheet Accounts, Area III Select Transactions) plus the Technical Accounting and Reporting and State and Local Governments areas of the BAR discipline — with the FASB Accounting Standards Codification and the GASB Codification as the primary texts. No affiliation with the AICPA, NASBA, FASB or GASB is claimed.
blocks.capstone: The reader can take any set of financial statements — a 10-K, a not-for-profit's audited statements, or a state's ACFR — identify the standard behind each material line, reproduce its measurement with the entries, reconcile a government's fund statements to its government-wide statements, and say which numbers rest on management's estimates and how far they could move.

blocks.title: Accounting II: Audit, Tax, Law and Analysis
blocks.subject: Accounting
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that turn a reader who can already read a 10-K into one who understands how it was audited, how the income behind it is taxed, what law binds the transactions inside it, and how a decision-maker takes it apart. Shaped on the AUD and REG core sections and the BAR discipline of the public CPA blueprint, the block assumes the FAR block (this subject's days 1–20) and year one, works every rule on a real filing, a real return or a real case, and closes the forty-lesson course with the reader doing the analysis himself.
blocks.modelled_on: The public AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (CPA Evolution edition effective January 2024, as updated January 2026) — the AUD and REG core sections and the BAR discipline section — together with the PCAOB Auditing Standards, the AICPA Professional Standards (AU-C, AT-C, AR-C and ET sections), the Internal Revenue Code and Treasury Regulations, and the Uniform Commercial Code. No claim of affiliation with the AICPA, NASBA or any board of accountancy.
blocks.capstone: Given a public company's EDGAR filings, the reader can pull the tagged facts himself, rebuild the ratios and a forecast, run the analytics an auditor would run over the ledger, say which findings would rise to a critical audit matter or a material weakness, compute the federal tax on the transactions and the people behind them for the current year with that year's brackets and limits, and name the contract, secured-lending and bankruptcy rules that decide what happens when the numbers fail.

blocks.title: Wealth Management I: The Household as a Balance Sheet
blocks.subject: Wealth Management
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that turn year one's finance into the practice of planning for one real household: the fiduciary process and the psychology of the client, cash flow, debt and reserves, education funding and the aid formulas, six lessons of insurance taken to the actuarial and tax bottom, household investment policy (asset location, loss harvesting, concentrated stock, Monte Carlo and sequence risk), equity compensation, and the individual income tax at depth. Every lesson carries its own time-value arithmetic and is worked on one named hypothetical household, the Hartwells of Bridgeville, Pennsylvania, at the IRS, SSA and Department of Education figures for the year the lesson runs (designed at the 2026 figures: 401(k) $24,500, IRA $7,500, gift exclusion $19,000, standard deduction $32,200 MFJ, HSA $8,750 family). Block 2 continues with retirement income, Social Security and Medicare, plan distributions, annuities and estate planning.
blocks.modelled_on: The CFP Board's public Principal Knowledge Topics, domains A (Professional Conduct and Regulation), B (General Principles of Financial Planning), H (Psychology of Financial Planning), C (Risk Management and Insurance Planning), D (Investment Planning) and E (Tax Planning), in the order a CFP Board-registered program teaches them, with the Internal Revenue Code, the annual IRS revenue procedures and the retirement-income research literature as the primary texts. No claim of affiliation with CFP Board.
blocks.capstone: Build the Hartwells' complete integrated plan for one tax year from the primary sources: order every dollar of savings capacity across the 401(k), HSA, PA 529, backdoor Roth and taxable account; decide traditional versus Roth on the marginal-rate arithmetic including Pennsylvania's treatment; bunch charitable gifts through a donor-advised fund under the 0.5%-of-AGI floor; stack capital gains and a Roth conversion to the top of the target bracket; and state the household's federal, NIIT and Pennsylvania liability before and after, with every limit and threshold cited to the revenue procedure for the run year.

blocks.title: Wealth Management II: Retirement, Estates and the Whole Plan
blocks.subject: Wealth Management
blocks.mission: Twenty lessons that finish the forty-lesson wealth-management course: retirement planning at depth (qualified plans, IRAs and conversions, RMDs, Social Security, Medicare, pensions and annuities, the decumulation literature, health and long-term care), estate planning at depth (wills and probate, trusts, the transfer taxes and portability, freezes, charitable instruments, business succession, Pennsylvania's inheritance tax), the special circumstances that break the standard plan, the ethics and regulation of advice, and a capstone that builds one named household's plan end to end. Every limit, bracket, premium, bend point and exclusion is stated for the year the lesson runs and re-verified that morning against the IRS, SSA, CMS and Pennsylvania primary sources.
blocks.modelled_on: The CFP Board's public Principal Knowledge Topics (Retirement Savings and Income Planning, Estate Planning, Risk Management and Insurance Planning, Tax Planning, Professional Conduct and Regulation), the Internal Revenue Code and Treasury regulations, the Social Security Act and POMS, Pennsylvania's Probate, Estates and Fiduciaries Code and Inheritance and Estate Tax Act, and the retirement-income research literature from Bengen (1994) onward — with no claim of affiliation with any credentialing body.
blocks.capstone: Build a complete financial plan for a named household — balance sheet and cash flow, retirement projection with a Roth-conversion window, Social Security and pension arithmetic from the formulas, a withdrawal and tax policy, the health and long-term-care line, the insurance ledger, the estate documents and the Pennsylvania inheritance-tax bill — with every threshold verified against that year's primary sources, and defend each recommendation under a fiduciary standard.

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Inference for investors: alpha, Sharpe ratios and the multiple-testing haircut
days.headline_hint: Sixty-four years to prove a fund manager is any good
days.focus: Hypothesis testing as it is actually used on track records and factor claims: tests of means, variances and correlations on return series, the sampling error of a Sharpe ratio, and the corrections for having searched many strategies before finding one. Assumes day 61's p-values and confidence intervals and day 132's list of backtest pathologies; here the pathologies get their formal fixes. Afterwards the reader can compute how long a track record must be before its alpha means anything, and discount a published t-statistic for the number of trials behind it.
parts: Sixty-four years to a t of two: the arithmetic of proving skill
Means, variances and correlations: the tests an analyst actually runs on a return series
The Sharpe ratio is an estimate, not a fact
Three hundred factors and a t-statistic of three
The deflated Sharpe ratio: how many backtests did you run?
What a rejected null does and does not license
worked_examples: Fidelity Magellan under Peter Lynch, May 1977–May 1990 (about 29% a year against the S&P 500's roughly 15%): the alpha t-statistic from monthly returns, and whether it survives a Bonferroni haircut across the mutual-fund universe of the day.

Lo (2002) standard error of the US market's Sharpe ratio on Mkt-RF from Kenneth French's data library, 1926–2025, with the iid and autocorrelation-adjusted versions and the resulting confidence interval.
Harvey, Liu and Zhu's 316 published factors and their t > 3.0 hurdle, applied to the t-statistics of HML and UMD computed from the French library since 1963.
Bailey and López de Prado's deflated Sharpe ratio for a strategy with a backtested annual Sharpe of 1.2 found after 200 trials on ten years of daily data.
sources: Harvey, Liu & Zhu (2016), '... and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns', Review of Financial Studies 29(1)
Lo (2002), 'The Statistics of Sharpe Ratios', Financial Analysts Journal 58(4)
Bailey & López de Prado (2014), 'The Deflated Sharpe Ratio', Journal of Portfolio Management 40(5)
DeFusco, McLeavey, Pinto & Runkle, Quantitative Investment Analysis, 4th ed. (CFA Institute Investment Series, 2020)
days.exam_map: CFA Level I Quantitative Methods — Hypothesis Testing; Parametric and Non-Parametric Tests of Independence

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Multiple regression and factor attribution
days.headline_hint: Buffett's alpha, run through a regression that says he is a factor
days.focus: Multiple linear regression as investors use it: factor regressions that decompose a return into exposures and alpha, the diagnostics (t, F, R-squared, adjusted R-squared), the three assumption failures that matter for financial data — heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, multicollinearity — and their robust-standard-error fixes, dummy variables, and logistic regression for a binary outcome. Assumes day 41's least-squares geometry and day 74's regression mechanics. Afterwards the reader can run and read a factor regression of any fund and know which reported t-statistics to trust.
parts: What a factor regression is asking, and why the coefficients are exposures
Reading the output: t, F, R-squared, and what alpha means when the regressors are portfolios
The three violations that matter — and the White and Newey–West repairs
Dummies and interactions: the January effect as a regression
Misspecification: omitted variables, overlapping returns and the predictive-regression bias
Logistic regression: the probability of a downgrade, not the size of one
worked_examples: Berkshire Hathaway's monthly returns 1976–2017 on Mkt-RF, SMB, HML, UMD, then adding BAB and QMJ, following Frazzini, Kabiller & Pedersen's 'Buffett's Alpha' (FAJ 2018): a Sharpe ratio of 0.79 and an alpha that stops being significant once quality and low-beta are in the regression.
ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), 2015–2025, on the Fama–French five factors plus momentum from the French library: strongly negative HML and RMW loadings and an alpha whose t-statistic does not clear two.
Keim's (1983) January effect refit as a month-dummy regression on the French SMB series, 1927–2025, and what the January coefficient's t-statistic has done since publication.
Shiller's CAPE predicting ten-year real S&P 500 returns, 1881–2025: the overlapping-observation problem, Newey–West with 120 lags, and the Stambaugh bias in the slope.
sources: Wooldridge, Introductory Econometrics: A Modern Approach, 7th ed. (2020)
Newey & West (1987), 'A Simple, Positive Semi-Definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix', Econometrica 55(3)
Fama & French (1993), 'Common Risk Factors in the Returns on Stocks and Bonds', Journal of Financial Economics 33(1)
Frazzini, Kabiller & Pedersen (2018), 'Buffett's Alpha', Financial Analysts Journal 74(4)
days.exam_map: CFA Level II Quantitative Methods — Basics of Multiple Regression and Underlying Assumptions; Evaluating Regression Model Fit and Interpreting Model Results; Model Misspecification

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Time series for the analyst: unit roots, cointegration and volatility clustering on real series
days.headline_hint: The ten-year yield does not remember where it has been; the dividend yield does
days.focus: Time-series modelling as the CFA curriculum applies it to real series — fitted, tested and read, with the theory left to its owners: trend versus random walk, AR(p) fitting and mean-reversion half-lives, the Dickey–Fuller unit-root test and the spurious regression it prevents, cointegration as the statistical definition of a pair, Engle's ARCH-LM test for volatility clustering and GARCH(1,1) stated and fitted without derivation, seasonality and structural breaks. Assumes day 103's realised-vs-implied volatility, day 108's curve mechanics and lesson 2's regression diagnostics. The state-space, Kalman and spectral theory that sits under these models belongs to the Mathematics block later in the year; nothing here depends on it. Afterwards the reader can tell which series can be forecast by their own past and which cannot, run an ADF test and an Engle–Granger regression on live data, and fit a GARCH(1,1) to a return series and read its persistence.
parts: Trends, random walks and the difference between them
Autoregression on real series: fitting AR(p), mean reversion and the half-life of a deviation
The unit-root test in practice: Dickey–Fuller on a policy rate, and why regressing one random walk on another lies
Cointegration: pairs trading has a statistical definition, and Engle–Granger is the test
Volatility clusters: the ARCH-LM test, GARCH(1,1) stated and fitted, and the persistence that makes the VIX forecastable
Seasonality, breaks and out-of-sample humility
worked_examples: SOFR (FRED series SOFR, daily since 3 April 2018) and the ten-year Treasury yield (FRED DGS10, monthly, 1962–2026): an AR(1) coefficient indistinguishable from one on both, the ADF test that fails to reject, and the first differences that are left — and why an administered rate that moves in steps on FOMC dates fails the test for a different reason than a traded yield does.
Shiller's S&P 500 dividend yield, 1871–2025: monthly AR(1) with phi near 0.98 and the implied half-life of roughly three years.

S&P 500 daily returns 1990–2025: Engle's ARCH-LM test on the squared residuals, then a GARCH(1,1) fit stated from the software output — alpha near 0.08, beta near 0.91, persistence near 0.99 — and the implied unconditional volatility set against the VIX.
Engle–Granger cointegration of Exxon Mobil and Chevron daily log prices 2015–2025: the residual's ADF statistic, the error-correction coefficient and the spread's half-life.
sources: DeFusco, McLeavey, Pinto & Runkle, Quantitative Investment Analysis, 4th ed. (CFA Institute Investment Series, 2020), 'Time-Series Analysis'

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Revenue quality: RPO and backlog, deferred revenue as a leading indicator, gross versus net, and the ASC 606 / IFRS 15 adjustments
days.headline_hint: Sixty billion dollars Microsoft has collected and is not yet allowed to call revenue
days.focus: The top line as an analyst reads it, in the CFA Financial Statement Analysis manner: where the five-step model leaves judgment to management, the remaining-performance-obligation and backlog disclosures rebuilt into bookings, the deferred-revenue roll-forward as a leading indicator of growth, principal-versus-agent as the choice that sets a company's margin and its multiple, the handful of differences between ASC 606 and IFRS 15 that matter for comparability, and the enforcement record's signatures turned into a scorecard with thresholds. Assumes day 29's five steps and day 133's red-flag list; the standard's own mechanics — allocation, over-time measurement, contract costs — are Accounting I's later in the year, and nothing here depends on them. Afterwards the reader can reconstruct a company's billings from its footnotes, grade the quality of its reported growth, and put a US and a European software company on the same revenue line.
parts: Where revenue recognition leaves judgment to management, and where the analyst looks for it
Remaining performance obligations and backlog: the bookings you can rebuild from a footnote
Deferred revenue as a leading indicator: billings, the roll-forward, and growth that arrives before the income statement
Gross or net: why Uber's revenue is a quarter of what its riders pay, and what the choice does to margins and multiples
ASC 606 against IFRS 15: the differences that matter for comparability, and the adjustment for each
A revenue-quality scorecard: DSO, deferred revenue versus revenue growth, RPO coverage, disclosures that change, and the enforcement record's signatures
worked_examples: Microsoft FY2024 10-K, Note 13: unearned revenue of $60.2 billion and $269 billion of commercial remaining performance obligations — rolling the unearned balance forward to rebuild the year's billings from $245.1 billion of revenue, and SAP's 2024 annual report (IFRS 15) 'current cloud backlog' of €18.1 billion set beside it as the disclosure that is not the same thing.

Salesforce fiscal 2025 (year ended 31 January 2025): revenue of $37.9 billion, remaining performance obligations of $63.4 billion and current RPO of $30.2 billion — current-RPO growth set against the following four quarters of reported revenue growth, the relationship the sell side trades on.

Uber 2023 10-K: gross bookings of $137.9 billion against revenue of $37.3 billion, where the principal/agent line falls for Mobility, Delivery and Freight, and the take-rate and EV/revenue multiple that move with it.

Under Armour's May 2021 SEC settlement: $408 million of orders pulled forward across six quarters from Q3 2015, the $9 million penalty, and the DSO and inventory signatures the practice left in the 10-Qs — the thresholds a screen would have needed to catch it.
sources: Robinson, Henry, Pirie & Broihahn, International Financial Statement Analysis, 4th ed. (CFA Institute Investment Series, 2020), 'Analyzing Income Statements' and 'Financial Reporting Quality'
Schilit, Perler & Engelhart, Financial Shenanigans, 4th ed. (McGraw-Hill, 2018)
FASB ASC 606 and IFRS 15, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (for reference), with the SEC Financial Reporting Manual on the disclosure requirements
SEC Press Release 2021-78 and the accompanying order (Under Armour, Inc., 3 May 2021); Microsoft Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal 2024, Note 13 (Unearned Revenue)

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Cash flow as the analyst reads it: the reconciliation, the free-cash-flow definitions and the conversion tests
days.headline_hint: Amazon publishes three free cash flows, and the honest one is the smallest
days.focus: Reading the statement of cash flows the way an analyst does: the indirect reconciliation line by line for what each line says about the business, stock-based compensation as a cost the add-back hides, investment that sits inside operating activities — capitalised software and interest, content spend, finance-lease principal — and the one comparability adjustment for where IFRS filers put interest, dividends and taxes; then free cash flow defined five ways, free cash flow to the firm and to equity among them, built from what a 10-K discloses, and the conversion tests that catch a definition drifting to flatter the number. Assumes day 22's three sections and day 25's accrual gap; the reconstruction of the statement from two balance sheets and ASC 230's classification rules are Accounting I's later in the year. Afterwards the reader can compute a comparable free cash flow for any two companies, build FCFF and FCFE from a filing, and detect a definition that has moved.
parts: Reading the indirect reconciliation: what each line says about the business, and the lines that hide investment
Stock-based compensation is a real cost that the cash-flow statement adds back
Capex, capitalised software, capitalised interest and finance leases: where investment hides
One adjustment for comparability: interest, dividends and taxes sit in different sections under IFRS, and the analyst moves them
Free cash flow defined five ways — the company's own, FCFF, FCFE, owner earnings and the levered–unlevered pair — and how each is built from what is disclosed
Conversion tests and cash-flow ratios: FCF yield, cash return on invested capital, burn-rate arithmetic, and the definition that drifted
worked_examples: Amazon 2023 10-K: net income of $30.4 billion to operating cash flow of $84.9 billion (stock-based compensation $24.0 billion, D&A $48.7 billion, working capital), then to Amazon's three published free-cash-flow lines — $36.8 billion at the headline, lower after finance-lease principal repayments.

Netflix 2023: cash paid for content ($13.1 billion) versus content amortisation ($14.2 billion), operating cash flow $7.3 billion, free cash flow $6.9 billion — an investment that lives inside operating activities.

Shell 2023 annual report (IFRS) against ExxonMobil's 2023 10-K (US GAAP): interest paid in financing versus operating activities, and the adjustment needed before their operating cash flows are comparable.
Boeing 2024 10-K: operating cash flow of −$12.1 billion, the working-capital and program drivers behind it, and the run-rate burn against year-end cash and marketable securities of $26.3 billion.
sources: FASB ASC 230, Statement of Cash Flows; IAS 7, Statement of Cash Flows
Mulford & Comiskey, Creative Cash Flow Reporting (Wiley, 2005)
Robinson, Henry, Pirie & Broihahn, International Financial Statement Analysis, 4th ed. (2020), chapters on cash-flow analysis
Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2023, 'Free Cash Flows' non-GAAP reconciliation

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Analyst adjustments for capitalised costs, useful lives, operating leases and impairment timing
days.headline_hint: Microsoft found $3.7 billion by deciding its servers would live two more years
days.focus: The long-lived-asset and lease disclosures turned into the adjustments an analyst makes before comparing two companies: reversing or imposing capitalisation so that a company expensing R&D and a company capitalising software sit on one line, recomputing earnings under a peer's useful lives, capitalising operating leases the way a rating agency does and restating EBITDA, leverage and fixed-charge cover, putting IFRS 16 and ASC 842 filers on the same expense pattern, and reading the signals that precede an impairment so the write-down is anticipated rather than reported. Assumes day 64's depreciation and day 73's leases and off-balance-sheet items; the capitalisation tests, the lease-classification criteria and the impairment mechanics themselves are Accounting I's later in the year, and nothing here depends on them. Afterwards the reader can restate any company's operating income, invested capital and net debt on a peer-comparable basis and defend each adjustment.
parts: Capitalise or expense: the line that moves earnings, cash flow and ROIC at once — and the analyst's reversal of it
Useful lives are estimates: recomputing earnings under a peer's depreciation schedule
Operating leases capitalised the way a rating agency does: the liability, the EBITDA it manufactures, and lease-adjusted leverage and coverage
One lease, three expense patterns: putting an IFRS 16 filer and an ASC 842 filer on the same line
Impairment timing: why write-downs arrive late and cluster, and the signals the analyst reads before the auditor does
The adjusted statements: operating income, invested capital and net debt restated, and the ROIC that survives
worked_examples: Microsoft's extension of server and network equipment lives from four to six years at the start of FY2023, disclosed as roughly $3.7 billion of FY2023 operating income, and Amazon's January 2025 shortening of a subset of servers from six to five years, estimated at about −$700 million for 2025 — each company's operating income recomputed under the other's assumption.

Alphabet 2024 10-K: $49.3 billion of research and development expensed — capitalised by the analyst with a five-year amortisable life after Damodaran, and the adjusted operating income, invested capital and return on invested capital that result.

Starbucks FY2024 10-K lease footnote: the operating-lease liability and right-of-use asset as reported, the operating-lease cost moved out of operating expenses into depreciation and interest, and the EBITDA, lease-adjusted debt/EBITDA and fixed-charge cover a Moody's-style adjustment produces — then the same adjustment run in reverse on Ryanair's FY2024 IFRS 16 statements to set it beside Delta Air Lines' 2023 ASC 842 figures.

Intel's third quarter of 2024: $3.1 billion of impairments and accelerated depreciation on manufacturing assets, mostly the Intel 7 node — the utilisation, gross-margin and capex-to-depreciation signals visible in the preceding four 10-Qs, and the return on invested capital before and after the charge.
sources: Robinson, Henry, Pirie & Broihahn, International Financial Statement Analysis, 4th ed. (CFA Institute Investment Series, 2020), 'Long-Lived Assets' and 'Financial Analysis Techniques'

Damodaran (1999), 'Research and Development Expenses: Implications for Profitability Measurement and Valuation' (NYU Stern working paper); Lev & Sougiannis (1996), 'The Capitalization, Amortization, and Value-Relevance of R&D', Journal of Accounting and Economics 21(1)
Moody's Investors Service, 'Financial Statement Adjustments in the Analysis of Non-Financial Corporations' (rating methodology; the lease and pension adjustments)
Microsoft Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal 2023, Note 1, and Amazon.com Form 10-K for 2024, Note 1 (changes in accounting estimate); Starbucks Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal 2024, Leases note

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: The rate reconciliation as a source of insight: valuation-allowance reversals, cash tax versus book tax, and Pillar Two
days.headline_hint: Tesla earned $5.9 billion in a quarter by changing its mind about the future
days.focus: The income-tax footnote read for what it tells a forecaster: the effective-rate reconciliation sorted into recurring and one-off items and turned into a forward tax rate, the valuation-allowance reversal as earnings that arrive from a change of mind and how to recast EPS without it, the deferred-tax roll-forward as the bridge from book tax to the cash tax a free-cash-flow forecast needs, the unrecognised-tax-benefit table read as a contingent liability, and the law as an input — §174, §163(j) and bonus depreciation after the 2025 rewrite, and the 15% Pillar Two floor. Assumes day 82's current-versus-deferred split and effective-versus-statutory rate; the balance-sheet method's computation and the recognition rules themselves are Accounting I's later in the year. Afterwards the reader can forecast a company's effective and cash tax rates from its footnote, recast reported earnings for a tax event, and price an uncertain position.
parts: The reported tax line is a blend: statutory, effective and the reconciliation between them, read item by item
Recurring or one-off: sorting FDII, research credits, foreign-rate differentials and stock-compensation windfalls into a forward rate
The valuation-allowance reversal: earnings from a change of mind, and the recast EPS
Cash tax versus book tax: the deferred-tax roll-forward as the bridge, and the cash-tax rate a free-cash-flow forecast needs
Uncertain positions as a contingent liability: reading the $28.9 billion Microsoft says it does not owe
The law as an input: §174, §163(j) and bonus depreciation after the 2025 rewrite, and Pillar Two's 15% floor under the low-tax structure
worked_examples: Tesla 2023 10-K: the fourth-quarter release of the US valuation allowance — a $5.9 billion one-time non-cash benefit, a full-year provision of about −$5.0 billion, a negative effective rate, and full-year net income of $15.0 billion recast without it.

Alphabet 2023 10-K rate reconciliation: 21% statutory to 13.9% effective ($11.9 billion on $85.7 billion of pre-tax income), with the FDII deduction worth 4.6 points and the research credit 1.8 — which items to carry into a forecast and the forward rate they produce.

Microsoft FY2024 10-K: the IRS Notices of Proposed Adjustment of $28.9 billion for 2004–2013 transfer pricing, the unrecognised-tax-benefit roll-forward, and what a settlement would do to cash versus earnings.

Cash tax against book tax at Amazon and Apple: the §174 capitalisation of domestic R&D for 2022–2024 and the deferred tax asset it created in Amazon's 2023 10-K, then the cash-tax swing when expensing returned under P.L. 119-21 (2025); and Apple's FY2024 10-K, where the $10.2 billion one-time charge for the EU State Aid decision lifted the effective rate to 24.1% and the Pillar Two disclosure says what a 15% floor does to a low-tax Irish structure from fiscal 2025.
sources: Robinson, Henry, Pirie & Broihahn, International Financial Statement Analysis, 4th ed. (CFA Institute Investment Series, 2020), 'Income Taxes'
FASB ASC 740, Income Taxes, and IAS 12 (for reference); OECD, Global Anti-Base Erosion Model Rules (Pillar Two), 2021, with the administrative guidance of 2023–2025
Internal Revenue Code §174, §163(j) and §168(k) as amended by P.L. 119-21 (2025)
Tesla, Inc. Form 10-K for 2023, Note 14 (Income Taxes); Alphabet Inc. Form 10-K for 2023, Note 14; Apple Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2024, Income Taxes note

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Economic pension expense, funded status as debt, share-based compensation as a real cost, and the diluted share count
days.headline_hint: IBM paid $16 billion to make a promise someone else's problem, and booked a $5.9 billion loss for it
days.focus: The two compensation footnotes converted into the numbers a valuation needs: the projected benefit obligation as a bond the company wrote and its deficit as debt, economic pension cost with the actual return on assets in place of the expected and the smoothing stripped out, settlements and risk transfers read for what they change and what they only recognise, share-based compensation put back into operating income and free cash flow as the cost it is, and the diluted share count rebuilt from unvested awards by the treasury-stock method so the dilution the buyback hides is counted. Assumes day 73's obligations, day 78's share-count mechanics and day 99's option pricing; the corridor, the attribution schedule and the Monte Carlo valuation of a market-condition award are Accounting I's later in the year. Afterwards the reader can treat a pension deficit as debt, restate pension cost on economic terms, and value a company per share on the share count it will actually have.
parts: The pension is a bond the company wrote: the obligation, its discount-rate sensitivity, funded status and the deficit as debt
Reported pension cost versus economic pension cost: stripping the expected return and the smoothing
Settlements and risk transfers as the analyst reads them: what IBM's $5.9 billion charge changed and what it only recognised
Share-based compensation is a real cost: grant-date fair value against value delivered, and putting it back into operating income and free cash flow
The diluted share count: the treasury-stock method, unvested RSUs, and the dilution the buyback hides
The adjusted statements: net debt with the pension deficit, EBIT after SBC, and per-share value on the true count
worked_examples: Boeing 2023 10-K pension footnote: the PBO, plan assets and funded status, the discount-rate and expected-return assumptions and the disclosed sensitivity of the obligation to a 25-basis-point change in the discount rate — then the deficit added to net debt, and the year's economic pension cost recomputed with the actual return on plan assets in place of the expected.

IBM, September 2022: about $16 billion of US pension obligations for roughly 100,000 participants transferred to Prudential and MetLife, funded from plan assets, and the $5.9 billion non-cash pre-tax settlement charge — accumulated losses recognised at once rather than a new cost, the funded status before and after, and how an analyst treats the charge in operating earnings and in the debt bridge.

Tesla's 2018 CEO Performance Award: about $2.3 billion of grant-date fair value across twelve tranches against the tens of billions the tranches were worth when they vested — the expense the income statement recorded versus the cost shareholders bore, and what the gap says about grant-date fair value as a measure of SBC for a market-condition award.
Amazon 2023 10-K: $24.0 billion of stock-based compensation, RSUs outstanding, and the diluted-share computation by the treasury-stock method — the dilution that the cash-flow add-back conceals.
sources: CFA Program Level II curriculum reading, 'Employee Compensation: Post-Employment and Share-Based'
Damodaran (2005), 'Employee Stock Options (ESOPs) and Restricted Stock: Valuation Effects and Consequences' (NYU Stern working paper)
Coronado & Sharpe (2003), 'Did Pension Plan Accounting Contribute to a Stock Market Bubble?', Brookings Papers on Economic Activity 2003(1)
FASB ASC 715 and ASC 718; IAS 19 and IFRS 2 (for reference); Tesla, Inc. Definitive Proxy Statement (DEF 14A), 8 February 2018, '2018 CEO Performance Award'

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: How acquisitions distort comparability: purchase-price allocation, goodwill in the equity base, equity-method income in EBITDA
days.headline_hint: Berkshire lost $22.8 billion in 2022, and nothing happened
days.focus: The four ways to own part of another company read for what each does to the reported numbers: fair-value marks that make headline earnings meaningless and the operating earnings recovered from them, equity-method income as a line with no cash that does not belong in EBITDA and a stake valued against its quoted price, the purchase-price allocation read for what the acquirer bought and the amortisation and step-ups that depress the next years' earnings, goodwill in the equity base and the ROE, ROIC and book value with and without it, and organic versus acquired growth with the non-controlling interest in the bridge. Assumes day 86's consolidation basics; the acquisition method's mechanics, VIE consolidation and the equity-method entries are Accounting I's later in the year, and nothing here depends on them. Afterwards the reader can separate operating earnings from mark-to-market noise, restate a serial acquirer's returns and growth, and value an equity-method stake against its market.
parts: Four ways to own a piece of another company, and what each one does to the reported numbers
Fair value through net income: why ASU 2016-01 made Berkshire's headline earnings meaningless, and the operating earnings recovered from them
Equity-method income: one line, no cash, the EBITDA it should not be in, and the stake valued against its quoted price
The purchase-price allocation as the analyst reads it: what the acquirer bought, the intangibles that get amortised, and the step-ups that depress the next years' earnings
Goodwill in the equity base: ROE, ROIC and book value with and without it, and what an impairment does and does not say
Organic versus acquired growth, pro forma comparability, and the non-controlling interest in the bridge from enterprise to equity value
worked_examples: Berkshire Hathaway 2022 annual report: a $22.8 billion net loss beside $30.8 billion of operating earnings — the Apple position marked through net income under ASU 2016-01, and the unrealised-gain line that reversed in 2023.

Berkshire's roughly 27% equity-method stake in Kraft Heinz: the $3.0 billion write-down in Q4 2018 after Kraft Heinz's own $15.4 billion goodwill and intangible impairment, the $3.8 billion write-down in Q2 2025, and the carrying value against quoted value each year between.

Microsoft FY2024 10-K purchase-price allocation for Activision Blizzard ($68.7 billion equity value, $95 a share in cash): the goodwill share of the price, the acquired intangibles and the amortisation they add to fiscal 2024 and 2025 operating expenses, the Activision revenue disclosed inside the year's growth, and Microsoft's return on invested capital with and without the goodwill.

Coca-Cola 2023 10-K: equity income from investees of about $1.7 billion against the market value of its stakes in Monster Beverage, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners and Coca-Cola FEMSA — the gap between the line and the holdings, the equity income removed from EBITDA, and the stakes added to the enterprise-to-equity bridge at market.
sources: CFA Program Level II curriculum reading, 'Intercorporate Investments'
Koller, Goedhart & Wessels (McKinsey & Company), Valuation: Measuring and Managing the Value of Companies, 7th ed. (Wiley, 2020), chapters on nonoperating items, goodwill and acquired intangibles
FASB ASC 320, 321, 323, 805 and 810 and ASU 2016-01; IFRS 3, IFRS 10 and IAS 28 (for reference)
Berkshire Hathaway Inc. 2022 Annual Report (Form 10-K) and the shareholder letter's operating-earnings reconciliation; Microsoft Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal 2024, Note 8 (Business Combinations)

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Ratio systems, DuPont decomposition and forensic screens
days.headline_hint: Eight ratios that would have flagged Enron, run on the company that flagged in 2024
days.focus: The five-way DuPont decomposition of ROE, cash-flow-based ratios and the accrual ratio, and the three classic forensic models — Beneish's M-score as a probit, Sloan's accrual anomaly, Altman's Z — with common-size analysis across time and peers, all applied on statements adjusted by lessons 4–9. Assumes day 127's ratio families and day 133's red-flag list. Afterwards the reader can decompose any company's ROE into its chosen strategy, compute an M-score from a 10-K, and know a screen's false-positive rate before acting on it.
parts: The five-way DuPont: tax burden, interest burden, margin, turnover, leverage — and what each company chooses
Cash-flow ratios and the accrual ratio: Sloan's finding that accruals predict returns
The Beneish M-score is a probit model: eight indices and the 1999 sample
Altman's Z and the distance to distress: what a discriminant function still knows
Common-size statements across time and peers: reading a drift in one line
Building the screen: thresholds, false positives, and what to do when a company trips it
worked_examples: Five-way DuPont on Apple FY2024 (net income $93.7 billion on year-end equity of $57.0 billion after years of buybacks), Costco FY2024 (margin near 3%, turnover above 3x) and Nvidia FY2025 — three routes to a high ROE, decomposed from the 10-Ks.
Beneish M-score for Super Micro Computer's FY2024, from the delayed 10-K filed in February 2025 after the auditor change: DSRI, GMI, AQI, SGI, DEPI, SGAI, TATA and LVGI against the −1.78 cut-off.
Sloan's accrual ratio, balance-sheet and cash-flow versions, for Tesla 2023, where a $5.9 billion non-cash tax benefit sits inside net income.
Altman Z for Boeing at year-end 2024 with shareholders' equity of −$3.9 billion (−$17.2 billion a year earlier), against the 1968 zones and the Z'' variant for non-manufacturers.
sources: Beneish (1999), 'The Detection of Earnings Manipulation', Financial Analysts Journal 55(5)
Sloan (1996), 'Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows about Future Earnings?', The Accounting Review 71(3)
Altman (1968), 'Financial Ratios, Discriminant Analysis and the Prediction of Corporate Bankruptcy', Journal of Finance 23(4)
Penman, Financial Statement Analysis and Security Valuation, 5th ed. (McGraw-Hill, 2013)

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Cost of capital at depth: betas, the equity risk premium, cost of debt and project-specific rates
days.headline_hint: Nobody knows the equity risk premium, and every valuation depends on it
days.focus: Every input to a discount rate, estimated three ways and argued: the risk-free rate as a choice, the equity risk premium by history, implication and survey, betas from regression, bottom-up peer unlevering and Hamada relevering, the cost of debt from a traded bond or a synthetic rating, country and size premia and the case against them, and divisional rates by the pure-play method. Assumes day 66's CAPM and WACC and lesson 2's regression. Afterwards the reader can build a defensible WACC for any company from its 10-K and market data and state the range, not just the point.
parts: The risk-free rate is a choice: which Treasury, which currency, and what to do with a term premium
The equity risk premium three ways — historical, implied, survey — and why they disagree by three points
Betas that mean something: regression, bottom-up, Hamada relevering and the Blume adjustment
Cost of debt without a bond: synthetic ratings from coverage, and what to do with convertibles and preferred
Country and size: sovereign spreads, Kroll's deciles, and the arguments against both
Project and divisional rates: the pure-play method, and why one WACC is wrong for a conglomerate
worked_examples: Apple's WACC from the FY2024 10-K and market data: $96.7 billion of term debt plus $10.0 billion of commercial paper, the yield on Apple's 4.300% notes due 2033, a five-year monthly regression beta against the S&P 500, and three equity-risk-premium choices — a range, not a number.

A bottom-up beta for Delta Air Lines: unlever the regression betas of United, American and Southwest using each carrier's 10-K debt including capitalised leases (lesson 6), average, and relever at Delta's own debt-to-equity.
The equity risk premium in 2026: the Kroll SBBI 1926–2025 arithmetic and geometric averages, Damodaran's January 2026 implied premium, and the Fernández survey — the same market, three numbers.
Petrobras's cost of equity with a country risk premium built from Brazil's sovereign CDS spread scaled by relative equity volatility, Damodaran's method, against the plain CAPM answer.

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Capital budgeting at depth: cash-flow construction, unequal lives, project risk and real options
days.headline_hint: The most valuable thing Intel did in Ohio was not build the fab yet
days.focus: Project appraisal as a corporate-finance professional does it: incremental after-tax cash flows with current depreciation law and government grants, inflation and working capital handled consistently, replacement chains and the equivalent annual annuity, sensitivity, scenario and Monte Carlo analysis with a project-specific hurdle rate, and real options — defer, expand, abandon — priced on a binomial lattice rather than added as a fudge. Assumes day 45's NPV and IRR, day 94's option payoffs and lesson 11's discount rates. Afterwards the reader can appraise a multi-billion-dollar capital project the way its board should, including the value of waiting.
parts: Building the project cash flows: incremental, after-tax, with 100% bonus depreciation and a CHIPS grant in year zero
Inflation, working capital and the terminal salvage that everyone gets backwards
Unequal lives: replacement chains and the equivalent annual annuity
Project risk: sensitivity, scenario, Monte Carlo — and the hurdle rate that is not the company's WACC
Real options: defer, expand, abandon — priced on a binomial lattice
Capital rationing, the profitability index, and why IRR still runs the boardroom
worked_examples: Micron's Boise, Idaho fab: the $15 billion project announced in 2022, the CHIPS Act award of up to $6.165 billion finalised in December 2024, 100% bonus depreciation restored by P.L. 119-21 for property acquired after 19 January 2025, a 21% federal plus 5.8% Idaho rate — the after-tax NPV and its sensitivity to DRAM pricing.

Equivalent annual annuity for a fleet choice: a new narrow-body at a realistic net price with a 25-year life against a ten-year life-extension of an older type, using Delta Air Lines' 2023 10-K fleet and capital-expenditure disclosures.

Intel's Ohio fab, pushed out to 2030–31: valued as an American option to defer, with the project's present value as the underlying and volatility from SOX index options, on a five-step binomial lattice.
An abandonment option on a copper mine: COMEX copper at the current front-month price, the mine's position on the cost curve, and the value of the right to shut, after Brennan & Schwartz (1985).

Trigeorgis, Real Options: Managerial Flexibility and Strategy in Resource Allocation (MIT Press, 1996)
Brennan & Schwartz (1985), 'Evaluating Natural Resource Investments', Journal of Business 58(2)
IRS Publication 946, How to Depreciate Property; IRC §168(k) as amended by P.L. 119-21 (2025)

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Capital structure: trade-off, pecking order, agency, market timing — and what the data say
days.headline_hint: Boeing's shareholders owned less than nothing, and the bond market still lent
days.focus: The theories of leverage beyond Modigliani–Miller — Miller's personal-tax correction, non-debt tax shields, the trade-off with measurable distress costs, pecking order from asymmetric information, agency and free cash flow, market timing — and the evidence from surveys, panel regressions and rating behaviour that decides between them. Assumes day 71's MM propositions and day 113's credit. Afterwards the reader can explain a company's leverage by which theory it fits, price the tax shield with adjusted present value, and identify the rating cliff that actually sets the target.
parts: Beyond Modigliani–Miller: the tax shield with personal taxes (Miller 1977) and non-debt shields (DeAngelo–Masulis)
The trade-off theory and the costs of distress you can actually measure
Pecking order: asymmetric information and why equity issues fall the day they are announced
Agency: free cash flow, debt as discipline, and the asset-substitution game
The evidence: Graham–Harvey, Frank–Goyal, rating targets and the cross-industry leverage table
Choosing a target: rating cliffs, §163(j), and Apple's decision to borrow $100 billion it did not need
worked_examples: Apple 2013–2024: term debt raised to over $100 billion against a larger offshore cash pile — the adjusted-present-value tax shield at 21% (35% before 2018), and what the 2017 repatriation tax did to the logic; FY2024 term debt of $96.7 billion.

Boeing: shareholders' equity of −$17.2 billion at end-2023, ratings one notch above junk, and the $24.25 billion October 2024 offering of common stock and mandatory convertible preferred — the price of staying investment grade.

Netflix's 5.875% senior notes due 2028: the yield path from high-yield issuance in 2018 to the investment-grade upgrades of 2021–2022, read as the market's charge for leverage falling as cash flow arrived.

Frank & Goyal's six core factors — industry median leverage, tangibility, size, market-to-book, profitability, expected inflation — refit on a hand-built 2024 sample from 10-Ks, against Damodaran's industry leverage table.

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Payout policy: dividends, repurchases, signalling, taxes and the arithmetic of accretion
days.headline_hint: Apple has bought back four shares in ten, and earnings per share noticed
days.focus: Why payout matters when Miller–Modigliani says it should not: taxes, signalling, clienteles and agency; Lintner's partial-adjustment model; the buyback arithmetic and the earnings-yield test that decides whether a repurchase adds value; the evidence on disappearing dividends and dividend–buyback substitution; and payout capacity read from free cash flow to equity. Assumes day 55's total return, day 78's share-count mechanics and lesson 13's leverage. Afterwards the reader can decompose EPS growth into earnings growth and share shrinkage, test a dividend's coverage, and read a policy change as the signal it is.
parts: Dividend irrelevance and its escape hatches: taxes, signalling, clienteles, agency
Lintner's model: why dividends are sticky and what a cut signals
Buybacks: the EPS arithmetic, the earnings-yield versus after-tax-cost-of-debt test, and when a buyback destroys value
Taxes: qualified dividends, the 1% excise, and the shareholder who sets the policy
The evidence: disappearing dividends, the substitution hypothesis, the buyback anomaly
Payout capacity: FCFE coverage, the dividend that outruns cash, and reading a policy from the 10-K
worked_examples: Apple FY2024 10-K: $94.9 billion of repurchases and $15.2 billion of dividends, and a split-adjusted share count from roughly 26 billion in 2013 to about 15 billion — decomposing 2013–2024 EPS growth into net-income growth and share shrinkage.
Meta's first dividend, $0.50 a quarter announced 1 February 2024 with fourth-quarter results, and the announcement-day return — signalling tested against a Lintner target payout.
AT&T's 2022 cut from $2.08 to $1.11 a share alongside the WarnerMedia spin-off: FCFE coverage before and after, and the yield the market demanded on the day.

Coca-Cola's dividend history 1990–2026 (64 consecutive increases; $2.12 annualised after the February 2026 raise to $0.53 a quarter) fit to Lintner's partial-adjustment model: the target payout ratio and the speed of adjustment.

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Mergers, acquisitions and restructuring: pricing, synergies, accretion, the financing mix, spin-offs and the Form 10
days.headline_hint: Exxon paid for Pioneer with paper, and the paper was the whole argument
days.focus: Deals as a strategic acquirer's corporate-finance decision: why they happen and the evidence that acquirers overpay, pricing a target as premium plus the synergy value it implies, cash versus stock and the exchange-ratio and accretion arithmetic, the financing mix and the rating an acquirer chooses to keep, restructuring by spin-off and carve-out — the Form 10, the when-issued market and the conglomerate discount — and the regulatory and defensive machinery. The leveraged-buyout model — sources and uses, the debt schedule, the exit bridge — is Finance & Markets II's private-equity lesson, not today's. Assumes day 75's transaction multiples, day 80's DCF, lesson 9's reading of acquisition accounting and lesson 13's debt capacity. Afterwards the reader can evaluate an announced deal — premium, synergies needed, accretion on both the GAAP and the adjusted count, financing, antitrust risk — from the merger proxy and two 10-Ks.
parts: Why deals happen: synergies, hubris, and the evidence that acquirers pay too much
Pricing the target: premium over the undisturbed price, the synergy value it implies, and who captures it
Cash or stock: the exchange ratio, accretion/dilution and the bootstrap illusion
The financing mix: cash on hand, new debt, new shares, and the rating the acquirer decides to keep
Restructuring: spin-offs, split-offs and carve-outs — the Form 10, the when-issued market and the sum-of-the-parts discount
Regulators and defences: HSR, the 2023 Merger Guidelines' HHI thresholds, poison pills and staggered boards
worked_examples: ExxonMobil–Pioneer Natural Resources, closed 3 May 2024: 2.3234 Exxon shares per Pioneer share, about $59.5 billion, an 18% premium to the undisturbed 5 October 2023 close — the exchange ratio, the post-deal ownership split, and 2024 EPS accretion from the two 10-Ks.

Broadcom–VMware, closed 22 November 2023: each VMware share elected $142.50 in cash or 0.2520 Broadcom shares, prorated to half cash and half stock overall; about $30.8 billion of cash and roughly 544 million new Broadcom shares, the cash funded with $30.4 billion of new term loans — accretion/dilution from the Form S-4 and Broadcom's fiscal 2024 10-K, where GAAP EPS was diluted by the amortisation of acquired intangibles while the company's non-GAAP EPS was accretive, and which of the two the acquirer's own presentation showed.

Microsoft–Activision Blizzard: $95 a share in cash, $68.7 billion, a 45% premium to the $65.39 close of 14 January 2022 — the annual after-tax synergy needed at Microsoft's cost of capital (lesson 11) to justify the premium, and the goodwill it produced (lesson 9).

General Electric's three-way split — GE HealthCare (January 2023) and GE Vernova (April 2024): the Form 10 each carried, the when-issued trading before separation, and the market value of the parts after separation against GE's capitalisation before the November 2021 announcement.
sources: Bruner, Applied Mergers and Acquisitions (Wiley, 2004)

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Industry and competitive analysis: structure, moats, cost curves and the persistence of returns
days.headline_hint: TSMC and Intel made the same thing in 2024, and only one of them made money
days.focus: The analysis that precedes any forecast: industry classification and lifecycle, Porter's five forces measured rather than listed (concentration by HHI, switching costs, cost curves), moats as ROIC-minus-WACC spreads and their fade rates, pricing power read from the gross-margin line across a cycle, and the marginal producer's economics. Assumes day 26's market structures and day 127's ratios, plus lesson 10's adjusted returns. Afterwards the reader can score a company's competitive position with numbers and translate it into the growth and margin fade that the valuation lessons need.
parts: Industry classification and the lifecycle: where the revenue pool is and how fast it is moving
Porter's five forces, done with numbers: concentration, switching costs, cost curves
Moats you can measure: ROIC minus WACC, its persistence, and the fade rate
Pricing power in the gross margin: what the memory cycle and the foundry duopoly say
Cost curves and the marginal producer: oil, memory, airlines
From industry to company: the competitive-position scorecard that feeds a forecast
worked_examples: HHI for US wireless after T-Mobile–Sprint (closed April 2020): Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile postpaid phone shares from their 2024 10-Ks against the 2023 Merger Guidelines' 1,800-point threshold and 100-point delta.

TSMC 2024 (gross margin about 56%) against Intel Foundry 2024 (operating loss of $13.3 billion on $17.3 billion of revenue): the foundry cost curve, scale and utilisation, and the return spread on the same node economics.
Micron's FY2023 net loss of $5.8 billion against its FY2025 results: the DRAM cycle as a pricing-power stress test on the gross-margin line.
ROIC-minus-WACC persistence, 2014–2024: Union Pacific against Delta Air Lines from their 10-Ks — a railroad duopoly and an airline oligopoly a decade apart.

days.subject: Finance & Markets
days.topic: Dividend discount models: Gordon, multistage, H-model, PVGO and implied expectations
days.headline_hint: Coca-Cola's price is a forecast of dividends no one alive will collect
days.focus: The dividend discount model taught to the bottom: the Gordon model as a geometric series, sustainable growth as a ceiling, two- and three-stage models and the H-model's linear fade, the present value of growth opportunities, and the model run backwards to extract the market's implied return or growth. Assumes day 35's discounting, day 55's dividends and day 80's DCF sensitivity, and lesson 11's cost of equity. Afterwards the reader can value a mature dividend payer three ways, state what fraction of any price is growth, and read a dividend yield as a forecast.
parts: A share is a perpetuity with a growth rate: the Gordon model and the geometric series inside it
Sustainable growth: g = b × ROE, and why it is a ceiling and not a forecast
Two-stage, three-stage and the H-model: smoothing the fade without lying about it
PVGO: how much of a price is the business that exists, and how much the business it must build
Running the model backwards: implied return, implied growth, and the market's forecast for Verizon
When the model applies, when it does not, and the spreadsheet mistakes that cost the most
worked_examples: Coca-Cola: $2.12 of annualised dividends after the February 2026 raise (the 64th consecutive increase), the current share price, and the growth rate the Gordon model implies at an 8% cost of equity — checked against the sustainable growth from KO's latest 10-K ROE and payout ratio.
Johnson & Johnson: a three-stage model from the current dividend, consensus five-year growth, a ten-year linear fade to 3%, and the share of total value sitting in the terminal stage.
PVGO for Nvidia against Coca-Cola: price minus forward EPS over the cost of equity — the fraction of each price that is growth rather than the business as it stands.
Verizon at its current dividend yield: the market-implied long-run growth at a 8.5% cost of equity, and what it says about the dividend's safety relative to FCFE (lesson 14).
sources: Gordon, The Investment, Financing, and Valuation of the Corporation (Irwin, 1962); Williams, The Theory of Investment Value (Harvard, 1938)
Fuller & Hsia (1984), 'A Simplified Common Stock Valuation Model', Financial Analysts Journal 40(5)
