days.topic: Software security fundamentals
days.headline_hint: Trusting trust: the principles from 1975 that still explain every breach, and the backdoor that nearly shipped in 2024
days.focus: Security as a discipline with principles, not a checklist. Saltzer and Schroeder's design principles (least privilege, complete mediation, fail-safe defaults, separation of privilege), threat modelling (assets, trust boundaries, STRIDE), the major vulnerability classes by mechanism (injection, broken access control, memory safety, deserialisation, SSRF, misconfiguration) mapped to the OWASP Top 10:2025 and CWE Top 25, authentication and secrets management, supply-chain security (dependency pinning, SBOMs, SLSA, the xz-utils backdoor), sandboxing mechanisms (namespaces, seccomp, gVisor, Firecracker), and CI/CD attack surface (pull_request_target, secrets in logs). Afterwards the reader can threat-model this repository and rank its exposures. refresh: check the current OWASP and CWE lists, the latest major supply-chain incident and current GitHub Actions hardening guidance before writing.
parts: Eight principles from 1975: Saltzer and Schroeder and why they have not aged
Drawing the threat model: assets, trust boundaries and STRIDE on a real system
The vulnerability classes: injection, access control, memory safety and deserialisation, by mechanism
Secrets and identity: tokens, rotation, the log that leaks and the environment variable that doesn't
The supply chain: pinning, SBOMs, SLSA and the xz-utils backdoor hour by hour
Sandboxes and pipelines: namespaces, seccomp, microVMs and the CI job that owns your repo
worked_examples: The xz-utils backdoor (CVE-2024-3094): the two-year maintainer social-engineering timeline, the build-script injection in 5.6.0/5.6.1, the sshd hook through liblzma, and the 500 ms login delay that led Andres Freund to it — as a supply-chain threat model

Threat-modelling this repository: trust boundaries between fetched web content, the routine, the repo, Actions and Telegram; the assets (secrets, the published site, the reader's phone); STRIDE per boundary; and how iron rules 1, 2, 3 and 6 map to specific mitigations
A GitHub Actions pwn-request: a pull_request_target workflow that checks out the PR head and runs its tests — the exact step that hands an attacker the repository token, and the two-line fix
Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228): the JNDI lookup string, the deserialisation path, and the CVSS 10.0 scoring worked field by field
sources: Saltzer and Schroeder, 'The Protection of Information in Computer Systems' (Proceedings of the IEEE, 1975); Thompson, 'Reflections on Trusting Trust' (CACM 1984)
OWASP Top 10:2025 (final release, January 2026); MITRE CWE Top 25 Most Dangerous Software Weaknesses (current year)
Agache et al., 'Firecracker: Lightweight Virtualization for Serverless Applications' (NSDI 2020); SLSA specification v1.0 (slsa.dev)
CISA and NIST advisories and the public technical analyses of CVE-2024-3094 (xz-utils) and CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell); GitHub Docs, 'Security hardening for GitHub Actions' (current)

days.subject: AI, Technology & Coding
days.topic: Security of AI systems: prompt injection, data poisoning, model theft and the defences that hold
days.headline_hint: Two hundred and fifty documents: the attack surface a language model adds to every system it touches
days.focus: The adversarial-machine-learning taxonomy applied to deployed models. Direct and indirect prompt injection (the lethal trifecta of private data, untrusted content and an exfiltration channel; EchoLeak's zero-click chain), jailbreaks and optimised suffixes (GCG), training-data poisoning with the near-constant-sample result, backdoors and sleeper triggers, training-data extraction and membership inference, model extraction and weight theft (including recovering an embedding layer through an API), and defence by architecture — CaMeL's separation of control and data flow, tool permissioning, output filtering, canaries, the limits of classifier guardrails; the OWASP LLM Top 10 and NIST AI 100-2 as the maps. Afterwards the reader can audit an LLM application for the trifecta and say which defences are structural and which are hopes. refresh: check the 2026 CVE and incident record for LLM applications, the current defence literature (CaMeL successors, the labs' injection benchmarks) and the current NIST and OWASP revisions before writing.
parts: The taxonomy: evasion, poisoning, privacy and abuse, from NIST AI 100-2 to the agent
Injection through the side door: indirect prompt injection and the lethal trifecta
Breaking the guard: jailbreaks, optimised suffixes and what a refusal classifier can't see
Poisoning the well: a near-constant number of documents, backdoors and sleeper triggers
Stealing the model: extraction, membership inference and the embedding layer over an API
Defence by construction: CaMeL, permissions, canaries and the difference between a filter and a boundary
worked_examples: EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711) reconstructed: the email that carried the instruction, the retrieval that surfaced it, the reference-style link that exfiltrated, and which leg of the trifecta each mitigation removes

Souly et al. (2025): 250 poisoned documents backdooring models from 600M to 13B parameters trained on 6B–260B tokens — the poison fraction at each scale (down to about 0.00016%) and why 'percentage of the corpus' was the wrong threat model
Carlini et al. (2024) recovering a production model's embedding projection: the rank of the logit matrix, the query count and the dollar cost the paper reports

Auditing this newspaper: fetched articles (untrusted), the routine's tools (repo write, git push) and the Telegram channel — the trifecta is present; iron rule 2 and the Actions-only sender examined as boundaries versus filters

sources: Greshake et al., 'Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection' (AISec 2023); Zou et al., 'Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models' (2023)

Souly et al., 'Poisoning Attacks on LLMs Require a Near-Constant Number of Poison Samples' (2025, arXiv:2510.07192); Hubinger et al., 'Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training' (2024)
Carlini et al., 'Stealing Part of a Production Language Model' (ICML 2024); Carlini et al., 'Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models' (USENIX Security 2021)

days.subject: AI, Technology & Coding
days.topic: AI safety and alignment as an engineering discipline
days.headline_hint: Thresholds, evals and the safety case: how alignment stopped being a philosophy seminar
days.focus: Alignment treated the way aerospace treats safety — hazards, controls, evidence. The threat models (misuse, misalignment, loss of control) stated so they can be tested; the frontier safety frameworks (capability thresholds, dangerous-capability evaluations for CBRN, cyber and autonomy, deployment and security standards tied to them, the safety-case form); reward hacking and specification gaming as the recurring failure; the empirical alignment results — sleeper agents surviving safety training, alignment faking, agentic misalignment in evaluation settings — and what they do and do not show; scalable oversight and weak-to-strong generalisation; interpretability as an engineering tool (superposition, sparse autoencoders, attribution graphs); and the regulatory layer (EU AI Act GPAI obligations, the NIST AI RMF). Afterwards the reader can read a system card and judge whether its safety case supports the deployment decision. refresh: check the current versions of the labs' safety frameworks and system cards, the current interpretability results and the state of EU AI Act GPAI enforcement before writing.
parts: Three ways it goes wrong: misuse, misalignment and loss of control, stated so they can be tested
The framework: capability thresholds, dangerous-capability evals and the safety case
The evidence so far: sleeper agents, alignment faking and agentic misalignment, read carefully
Oversight that scales: debate, weak-to-strong and the limits of a human grader
Looking inside: superposition, sparse autoencoders and attribution graphs
The law arrives: EU AI Act GPAI obligations, NIST's framework and what a system card must now say
worked_examples: A current frontier system card read as a safety case: the capability thresholds it names, the eval results against each, the security and deployment standard invoked, and the residual-risk statement — with the two places the argument is weakest

Alignment faking (Greenblatt et al. 2024): the compliance rate in the monitored condition, the scratchpad evidence of strategic reasoning, the rise to 78% after the RL setup, and what the design can and cannot rule out

Sparse-autoencoder arithmetic from Scaling Monosemanticity: a residual stream into a 34-million-feature dictionary — the L0, reconstruction loss and dead-feature fraction as reported, and the compute of training the SAE

The EU AI Act's GPAI provisions (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Articles 51–55): the 10^25 FLOP systemic-risk presumption applied to Llama 3 405B's reported ~3.8 × 10^25 training FLOPs, and the obligations that follow
sources: Anthropic, Responsible Scaling Policy (current version) and the latest Claude system card; OpenAI, Preparedness Framework (current); Google DeepMind, Frontier Safety Framework (current)
Hubinger et al., 'Sleeper Agents' (2024); Greenblatt et al., 'Alignment Faking in Large Language Models' (2024); Burns et al., 'Weak-to-Strong Generalization' (2023)

Templeton et al., 'Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet' (2024); Lindsey et al., 'On the Biology of a Large Language Model' (2025); Elhage et al., 'Toy Models of Superposition' (2022)

Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act), Chapter V on general-purpose AI models; NIST AI 100-1, 'Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0' (2023); Amodei et al., 'Concrete Problems in AI Safety' (2016)

days.subject: AI, Technology & Coding
days.topic: Language models and text as alternative data: 10-Ks, earnings calls, embeddings and the LLM-as-analyst evidence
days.headline_hint: When is a liability not a liability? What language models have actually found in filings and earnings calls, and the look-ahead that only a text corpus can hide
days.focus: The capstone, narrowed to the one dataset this newspaper handles every morning: text. Year-one day 145 surveyed machine learning in markets and block 2's day 20 owns the strategy protocol — the deflated Sharpe ratio, purged cross-validation, cost realism — so this lesson cites both and re-teaches neither; it does what is specific to language. Dictionaries and why finance needed its own (Loughran–McDonald against the Harvard list, and the three-quarters of 'negative' hits that were not); the filing as a vector — TF-IDF, cosine and Jaccard similarity, Cohen, Malloy and Nguyen's finding that a changed 10-K is the signal, and Hoberg–Phillips's text-based industries that redraw the peer map from Item 1; embeddings — word2vec on two hundred thousand earnings calls, sentence embeddings and Chen, Kelly and Xiu's LLM news representations; the LLM-as-analyst record — Kim, Muhn and Nikolaev's anonymised financial statements, Lopez-Lira and Tang's post-cutoff headlines, Jha et al.'s call-transcript investment scores — read with day 9's error bars; then the look-ahead traps unique to text, at both levels: the pre-trained model that has already read the sample (Glasserman and Lin's name-masking test, post-cutoff samples, chronologically consistent language models) and the corpus that leaks (dictionaries fitted on the full sample, amended filings overwriting the original, edited transcripts, supervised sentiment trained on the returns it predicts, and the regime changes in filing language after Reg FD, Item 1A and XBRL). Afterwards the reader can build a text signal from EDGAR and a transcript feed, test it for both kinds of look-ahead, and hand it to block 2's protocol without fooling himself. refresh: check the current published results on LLMs and return prediction, the chronologically-consistent-model literature and the labs' current training-cutoff disclosures before writing.
parts: Not a liability: why finance needed its own dictionary, and what a word count still predicts
The filing as a vector: similarity measures, Lazy Prices and the industries that 10-Ks draw for themselves
Embeddings and the earnings call: word2vec on two hundred thousand transcripts to the LLM reading the Q&A
The model as analyst: an anonymised balance sheet, a post-cutoff headline and what the accuracy actually means
The model has read the future: look-ahead through pre-training and the three designs that rule it out
The corpus leaks too: fitted dictionaries, amended filings, edited transcripts — and the hand-off to block 2's protocol
worked_examples: Loughran–McDonald applied to Apple's Form 10-K for fiscal 2024 (CIK 320193, filed 2024-11-01, from EDGAR full text): negative-word counts under the Harvard General Inquirer list and the LM list, the share of the Harvard count coming from finance-neutral words such as 'liability', 'tax', 'cost' and 'capital' — set against the 2011 paper's finding that almost three-quarters of Harvard's negative hits in 10-Ks are such words — and the two sentiment scores as fractions of total words

Lazy Prices reproduced on one firm: cosine, Jaccard, minimum-edit-distance and simple similarity between the Item 1A and Item 7 sections of Apple's fiscal 2023 and 2024 10-Ks, the quintile of the paper's changer/non-changer distribution the numbers fall into, and the paper's reported long-non-changer/short-changer alpha (up to 188 basis points a month) with its inattention explanation; then Hoberg–Phillips: TF-IDF cosine similarity of the Item 1 descriptions of NVIDIA (fiscal 2025) against AMD and against Kroger, next to their SIC codes (3674, 3674, 5411)

Kim, Muhn and Nikolaev in miniature: Apple's standardised, anonymised income statement and balance sheet for fiscal 2023–2024 from EDGAR's companyfacts JSON, the paper's chain-of-thought prompt, the model's direction call for fiscal 2025 earnings against the actual outcome — and then the paper's aggregate result (about 60% directional accuracy, against roughly 53–57% for analysts and a trained neural network's ~60%) with the binomial standard error from day 9 that says what one firm's answer is worth (nothing)

A look-ahead test on this newspaper's own archive: 200 dated headlines from site/reports/index.json scored by a current model with company names present and with names masked, the next-day-return correlation of each (from the run's price source), the gap as the memorisation measure following Glasserman and Lin, and the fraction of the sample that falls before the model's published training cutoff — with Lopez-Lira and Tang's post-cutoff design and a chronologically consistent model as the two clean alternatives
sources: Loughran and McDonald, 'When Is a Liability Not a Liability? Textual Analysis, Dictionaries, and 10-Ks' (Journal of Finance, 2011) and 'Textual Analysis in Accounting and Finance: A Survey' (Journal of Accounting Research, 2016); Gentzkow, Kelly and Taddy, 'Text as Data' (Journal of Economic Literature, 2019)

Cohen, Malloy and Nguyen, 'Lazy Prices' (Journal of Finance, 2020); Hoberg and Phillips, 'Text-Based Network Industries and Endogenous Product Differentiation' (Journal of Political Economy, 2016); Li, Mai, Shen and Yan, 'Measuring Corporate Culture Using Machine Learning' (Review of Financial Studies, 2021)

Lopez-Lira and Tang, 'Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models' (2023); Kim, Muhn and Nikolaev, 'Financial Statement Analysis with Large Language Models' (2024); Chen, Kelly and Xiu, 'Expected Returns and Large Language Models' (2022); Ke, Kelly and Xiu, 'Predicting Returns with Text Data' (2019)

Glasserman and Lin, 'Assessing Look-Ahead Bias in Stock Return Predictions Generated by GPT Sentiment Analysis' (2023); He, Lv, Manela and Wu, 'Chronologically Consistent Large Language Models' (2025); Sarkar and Vafa, 'Lookahead Bias in Pretrained Language Models' (2024); SEC EDGAR full-text search and the companyfacts API (data.sec.gov)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: The conceptual framework and the standard-setting machine
days.headline_hint: Before a single number is booked, someone decided what counts — the architecture beneath every 10-K
days.focus: Year one's day 3 said what accounting is for; this lesson takes the FASB's Concepts Statement 8 to the bottom: the objective, the qualitative characteristics, the elements, and the competing measurement bases that decide whether a line is cost, amortised cost or fair value. It then follows the rules to their makers — the FASB's due process and the Codification's hierarchy (ASC 105), the SEC's authority through Regulation S-X and Staff Accounting Bulletins — and applies materiality (SAB 99, SAB 108), the presentation standards (ASC 205, 210, 220) and ASC 250's three ways a company changes its own numbers. Afterwards the reader can read a change-in-accounting note or a revision of prior periods and say exactly which category it is and why the entries land where they do.
parts: What a financial statement is for, and who it is for: the objective and the qualitative characteristics
Assets, liabilities and the rest: the elements, recognition, and the measurement bases that compete for every line
Who writes the rules: the FASB's due process, the Codification's hierarchy and where the SEC's authority begins
Net income is not the last line: comprehensive income, OCI and the going-concern assessment
How big is material? SAB 99, SAB 108 and the rollover-versus-iron-curtain problem
Changing your mind on the record: ASC 250 — a new principle, a new estimate, or an error
worked_examples: Berkshire Hathaway's 2022 10-K: a $22.8 billion GAAP net loss beside $30.8 billion of operating earnings, traced to ASU 2016-01's fair-value-through-net-income rule for equity securities — measurement basis as the whole story

Macy's fiscal 2024 10-K: two ASC 250 events in one filing — the change from the LIFO retail method to the LIFO cost method as a change in accounting principle (with the auditor's preferability paragraph), and the $151 million of concealed small-package delivery expense (Q4 2021 to Q3 2024) evaluated under SAB 99 and SAB 108 and corrected by revising prior periods rather than a 'Big R' restatement

Microsoft's fiscal 2023 10-K: extending the useful lives of server and network equipment from four to six years, a change in estimate applied prospectively under ASC 250-10-45-17, adding about $3.7 billion to that year's operating income
Apple's fiscal 2024 statement of comprehensive income: the foreign currency translation, unrealised AFS and cash-flow-hedge lines that never touch net income, and the accumulated OCI roll-forward
sources: FASB Concepts Statement No. 8, Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting (chapters 1–8, as amended through 2024)
FASB ASC 105 (GAAP hierarchy), ASC 205, ASC 220 (Comprehensive Income) and ASC 250 (Accounting Changes and Error Corrections)
SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 99 (Materiality, 1999) and SAB No. 108 (Quantifying Misstatements, 2006)
Kieso, Weygandt & Warfield, Intermediate Accounting, 18th ed. (Wiley, 2022), chs. 1–2, 4 and 22
days.exam_map: FAR Area I (Financial Reporting): conceptual framework, standard-setting and general-purpose financial statements; FAR Area III (Select Transactions): accounting changes and error corrections

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Revenue under ASC 606, part one: contract, obligations, price
days.headline_hint: A sale is not a number until you have found the promises inside it — the first three steps of ASC 606
days.focus: Year one's day 29 taught when a sale becomes revenue; this lesson takes steps one to three of ASC 606 to the bottom. Step one: the five contract criteria, the collectibility threshold, combining contracts and the modification that is really a new contract. Step two: what makes a promise distinct, the series provision, assurance versus service warranties and the customer option that is a material right. Step three: variable consideration by expected value or most likely amount, the constraint, refund liabilities, the significant financing component, noncash consideration and consideration payable to a customer. Afterwards the reader can take a pharmaceutical sale with rebates and chargebacks or a subscription with a discounted renewal and write down the transaction price with its constraint.
parts: What makes a contract a contract: the five criteria, collectibility, and the modification that is really a new contract
Finding the promises: distinct goods and services, the series, warranties and the option that is a material right
Pricing what you cannot yet know: variable consideration, expected value, most likely amount, and the constraint
Money with a time cost: the significant financing component, noncash consideration and payments to the customer
Gross to net: how a drugmaker turns $100 of list price into roughly half that much revenue
worked_examples: Pfizer's 2023 10-K revenue note: the accruals for chargebacks, rebates, sales allowances and returns treated as variable consideration under the expected-value method, and the balance-sheet accounts they sit in

Microsoft's fiscal 2024 10-K revenue policy: Windows OEM licences at a point in time, Microsoft 365 subscriptions over time, the separate performance obligations inside one enterprise agreement, and a mid-term modification accounted for prospectively

Costco's fiscal 2024 10-K: membership fees deferred and recognised ratably over the twelve-month term, with the one-year practical expedient and the test for whether a financing component is significant

Alnylam Pharmaceuticals' 2023 10-K: the Roche collaboration's upfront payment and development milestones, the milestones constrained until the uncertainty resolves, and a $1 million equipment sale with a 20% chance of a $100,000 penalty priced by both variable-consideration methods
sources: FASB ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (ASU 2014-09 as amended), esp. 606-10-25 (contract and performance obligations) and 606-10-32 (transaction price)
FASB/IASB Joint Transition Resource Group for Revenue Recognition, staff memos and meeting summaries (2014–2016)
PwC, Revenue from contracts with customers (accounting guide), current edition
Kieso, Weygandt & Warfield, Intermediate Accounting, 18th ed. (Wiley, 2022), ch. 18
days.exam_map: FAR Area III (Select Transactions): revenue recognition — the five-step model and variable consideration; BAR Area II (Technical Accounting and Reporting): revenue recognition

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Revenue under ASC 606, part two: allocation, satisfaction, agents and costs
days.headline_hint: Uber never sells you a ride, and Salesforce spreads a salesman's commission over years — the back half of ASC 606
days.focus: Steps four and five and everything ASC 606 hangs on them. Allocation on relative standalone selling prices (adjusted market, expected cost plus margin, the residual approach) and where discounts and variable amounts land. Satisfaction over time — the three criteria, input and output methods, uninstalled materials — versus the point-in-time indicators of control. Then the judgments that decide a company's top line: principal versus agent, functional versus symbolic licences and the royalty exception, repurchase agreements, bill-and-hold and consignment, the incremental costs of obtaining a contract under ASC 340-40, and the balance-sheet presentation of contract assets, receivables and contract liabilities. Afterwards the reader can rebuild a software company's deferred revenue roll-forward and judge whether a marketplace's gross or net presentation is right.
parts: Splitting the price: standalone selling prices, the residual approach, and where discounts land
Over time or at a point: the three criteria, measuring progress, and what 'control' actually means
Whose sale is it? Principal, agent and the net-revenue question at Uber and Amazon
Licences and royalties: the right to use versus the right to access
The cost of winning a contract: ASC 340-40 and the capitalised commission
What the balance sheet shows: contract assets, contract liabilities and the remaining-performance-obligation disclosure
worked_examples: Uber's 2023 10-K: Mobility revenue presented net as an agent, the control indicators the note relies on, and the effect on the ratio of gross bookings to revenue; beside it, Amazon's third-party seller services recorded net
Salesforce's fiscal 2024 10-K: capitalised costs to obtain revenue contracts (sales commissions), the amortisation period chosen and the balances, walked through both statements

Boeing's 2023 10-K: over-time revenue on defence contracts by the cost-to-cost input method, point-in-time revenue on commercial aircraft delivery, and the reach-forward loss on the KC-46 programme as a contract-level loss provision

Microsoft's fiscal 2024 10-K: the remaining performance obligation disclosure, the portion expected within twelve months, and the contract liability roll-forward from opening balance to revenue recognised
sources: FASB ASC 606-10-32-28 to 32-41 (allocation), 606-10-25-23 to 25-37 (satisfaction), 606-10-55-36 to 55-40 (principal versus agent) and 606-10-55-54 to 55-65 (licensing)
FASB ASC 340-40, Other Assets and Deferred Costs — Contracts with Customers
ASU 2016-08 (Principal versus Agent Considerations) and ASU 2016-10 (Identifying Performance Obligations and Licensing)
Spiceland, Nelson & Thomas, Intermediate Accounting, 11th ed. (McGraw Hill, 2022), ch. 6
days.exam_map: FAR Area III: revenue recognition — allocation and satisfaction of performance obligations; BAR Area II: revenue recognition (principal versus agent, licensing, contract costs)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Inventory at depth: LIFO reserves, dollar-value LIFO and the retail method
days.headline_hint: Caterpillar's balance sheet is $3.4 billion light on purpose — the arithmetic behind the LIFO reserve
days.focus: Year one's day 30 taught FIFO, LIFO and weighted average; this lesson takes ASC 330 to practitioner level. What cost includes and excludes, and how periodic versus perpetual changes a LIFO answer. The LIFO reserve and how an analyst converts a LIFO company to FIFO (income, taxes, equity, the current ratio), the LIFO liquidation that gives back deferred tax, and the LIFO conformity rule. Dollar-value LIFO with price indices, pools and layers — the method large LIFO users actually run. The two write-down regimes that now coexist (lower of cost or net realisable value for FIFO and average cost; lower of cost or market with ceiling and floor for LIFO and retail), the retail inventory method with markups and markdowns, the gross-profit method, purchase-commitment losses and the self-correcting inventory error. Afterwards the reader can restate a LIFO filer to FIFO and run a dollar-value LIFO computation across several years.
parts: What cost is: ASC 330's boundary between product cost and period cost, and the perpetual-periodic difference that changes LIFO
The LIFO reserve: converting Caterpillar to FIFO, the tax that LIFO defers, and the liquidation that gives it back
Dollar-value LIFO: pools, price indices and layers — the method most large LIFO users actually run
Floors, ceilings and net realisable value: the two write-down regimes that now coexist
Counting without counting: the retail method Macy's just abandoned, and the gross-profit method after the warehouse fire
worked_examples: Caterpillar's 2023 10-K, Note 1.C: LIFO for about 65% of inventories, and the disclosure that inventories would have been $3,423 million higher under FIFO ($3,321 million a year earlier) — converting cost of sales, pre-tax income, deferred taxes, equity and the current ratio
A four-year dollar-value LIFO computation with a base-year index of 1.00 rising to 1.21: layers created, a liquidation in year three, and the reported cost of goods sold each year with the entries

Macy's fiscal 2023 10-K (LIFO retail inventory method) and its fiscal 2024 change to the LIFO cost method: the cost-to-retail ratio with markups and markdowns, a conventional-retail lower-of-cost-or-market calculation, and why a retailer would abandon the method
Kroger's fiscal 2023 10-K: the annual LIFO charge or credit in cost of sales, and a gross-profit-method estimate of inventory destroyed in a distribution-centre loss for an interim period
sources: FASB ASC 330, Inventory (incl. ASU 2015-11, Simplifying the Measurement of Inventory)
Internal Revenue Code §472 and Treas. Reg. §1.472-8 (dollar-value LIFO and the conformity requirement)
Kieso, Weygandt & Warfield, Intermediate Accounting, 18th ed. (Wiley, 2022), chs. 8–9
Caterpillar Inc., Form 10-K for fiscal 2023, Note 1.C (Inventories)
days.exam_map: FAR Area II (Select Balance Sheet Accounts): inventory

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Fair value (ASC 820) and investments: AFS, HTM, equity securities and CECL
days.headline_hint: Silicon Valley Bank was solvent on paper the day it died — the accounting that let $15 billion of losses hide in plain sight
days.focus: Fair value measurement and the investment standards that depend on it. ASC 820: the exit-price definition, principal market, the market, income and cost approaches, the Level 1/2/3 hierarchy, the Level 3 roll-forward and unobservable-input disclosures, the NAV practical expedient and the fair value option. ASC 320's three buckets for debt securities — trading, available-for-sale through OCI with recycling, held-to-maturity at amortised cost — and the tainting and transfer rules; ASC 321's fair-value-through-income rule for equity securities and the measurement alternative. Then ASC 326: the current expected credit loss model for loans, receivables and HTM securities (aging, PD/LGD, discounted cash flow and vintage methods, macro scenarios), the allowance model for AFS credit losses, and purchased credit-deteriorated assets. Afterwards the reader can classify a bank's securities book, rebuild an allowance roll-forward and explain SVB's balance sheet.
parts: What fair value means: the exit price, the principal market and the three approaches
Levels 1, 2 and 3: the hierarchy, the Level 3 roll-forward and the NAV expedient
Three buckets for a bond: trading, available-for-sale and held-to-maturity, and the accounting cost of each
Equity securities after ASU 2016-01: fair value through income, and the measurement alternative
CECL: from incurred loss to expected loss, and how an allowance is actually built
The bank that was solvent at amortised cost: SVB's 2022 balance sheet
worked_examples: SVB Financial Group's 2022 10-K (filed 24 February 2023): $91.3 billion of held-to-maturity securities at amortised cost with roughly $15 billion of unrealised losses disclosed only in the footnote, the AFS book marked through OCI, and the tangible-equity arithmetic if the HTM book were marked

JPMorgan Chase's 2023 10-K: the allowance for credit losses roll-forward for the card portfolio, the weighted macroeconomic scenarios behind the lifetime estimate, and the day-one allowance on the loans purchased from First Republic
A $10 million 4% bond bought at 96 to yield about 5%: the effective-interest table, the year-end AFS mark through OCI with its deferred tax, and the same bond after a transfer to held-to-maturity
Blackstone's 2023 10-K fair value tables: Level 3 investments, the unobservable inputs disclosed (discount rates, exit multiples), and the Level 3 roll-forward from opening balance to closing
sources: FASB ASC 820, Fair Value Measurement; ASC 320, Investments — Debt Securities; ASC 321, Investments — Equity Securities; ASC 326, Financial Instruments — Credit Losses (ASU 2016-13)
ASU 2016-01, Recognition and Measurement of Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities
Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Review of the Federal Reserve's Supervision and Regulation of Silicon Valley Bank (April 2023)
Kieso, Weygandt & Warfield, Intermediate Accounting, 18th ed. (Wiley, 2022), ch. 17
days.exam_map: FAR Area II: investments (debt and equity securities) and trade receivables (CECL); FAR Area III: fair value measurements

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: PP&E at depth: what to capitalise, capitalised interest, AROs and ASC 360 impairment
days.headline_hint: A power plant's cost includes the interest on the money that built it and the price of tearing it down — capitalisation to the bottom
days.focus: Year one's day 64 taught depreciation as an estimate; this lesson takes the asset's whole life under ASC 360. What is capitalised and what is expensed, betterments versus repairs, and the capitalisation cliff. Capitalised interest under ASC 835-20 — avoidable interest, weighted-average accumulated expenditures, specific versus general borrowings — and its regulated cousin AFUDC. Asset retirement obligations under ASC 410-20: fair value at inception, accretion, the capitalised retirement cost and revisions. The held-and-used impairment test (recoverability on undiscounted cash flows, then fair value, at the asset-group level, never reversed), held-for-sale measurement, discontinued operations under ASC 205-20, nonmonetary exchanges with and without commercial substance, and internal-use software under ASC 350-40. Afterwards the reader can compute avoidable interest, carry an ARO from inception to settlement, and run a real ASC 360 test.
parts: What belongs in the asset: directly attributable cost, betterments versus repairs, and the capitalisation cliff
Interest as a cost of the asset: avoidable interest, weighted-average accumulated expenditures and AFUDC at a utility
The cost of leaving: asset retirement obligations, accretion and the capitalised retirement cost
Is it still worth what we say? The ASC 360 recoverability test, the asset group and the fair-value write-down
Held for sale and discontinued operations: when depreciation stops and the business moves below the line
Software you build for yourself, and swaps with and without commercial substance
worked_examples: Duke Energy's 2023 10-K: allowance for funds used during construction with its debt and equity components, and an avoidable-interest calculation for a $600 million plant financed by a 5% construction loan plus general 4% debt, with the capitalised-interest entries

ExxonMobil's 2023 10-K asset retirement obligations roll-forward — accretion, liabilities incurred, settled and revised — and the balance sheet and income statement of a single well from drilling to plugging

Macy's fiscal 2024 10-K: long-lived asset impairments on underperforming stores under ASC 360, with the recoverability test run at store (asset-group) level and the fair value from discounted store cash flows

Johnson & Johnson's 2023 10-K: Kenvue presented as discontinued operations after the August 2023 exchange offer, the $21.0 billion gain recorded within net earnings from discontinued operations, and the strategic-shift test that put it there

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Intangibles and goodwill: amortisation, R&D and the ASC 350 impairment test
days.headline_hint: Kraft Heinz wrote $15 billion off brands it never stopped selling — how a goodwill impairment is actually computed
days.focus: The three kinds of intangible and the different test each faces. Finite-lived intangibles amortised and tested under ASC 360; indefinite-lived intangibles tested annually at fair value; goodwill assigned to reporting units and tested under ASC 350 as amended by ASU 2017-04 — the qualitative screen, the single quantitative step, interim triggers, the simultaneous-equation adjustment for tax-deductible goodwill and the private-company amortisation alternative. Research and development under ASC 730, in-process R&D acquired in a combination, software to be sold under ASC 985-20 and technological feasibility. The valuation methods the notes name — relief from royalty, multi-period excess earnings — worked with real inputs. Afterwards the reader can reproduce an impairment charge from a reporting unit's projections and read the three largest write-downs of recent years from their footnotes.
parts: Three kinds of intangible: finite, indefinite and goodwill — and why each is tested differently
Research is an expense, development is a fight: ASC 730, ASC 985-20 and in-process R&D
The reporting unit: where goodwill lives, and how a fair value is built for something that is not for sale
The test: qualitative screen, the single quantitative step, and the tax-deductible-goodwill iteration
Kraft Heinz, Verizon and Walgreens: three impairments read from the footnotes

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Leases, lessee side: classification, the discount rate and the two expense patterns
days.headline_hint: Dollar General owes more than $11 billion for buildings it does not own — the lessee's book under ASC 842
days.focus: Year one's day 73 said where leases hide; this lesson builds the lessee's book under ASC 842 from the contract up. Identifying a lease (an identified asset, the right to control), separating lease and non-lease components, the lease term with options reasonably certain, which payments count (fixed, in-substance fixed, index-linked, residual value guarantees), and the discount rate — the rate implicit, the incremental borrowing rate and how a retailer actually derives one. The five classification tests, initial measurement of the liability and right-of-use asset, and the two subsequent patterns: finance (interest plus amortisation, front-loaded) and operating (a single straight-line cost with the ROU asset as the plug). Remeasurement and modification, ROU impairment, the short-term election, presentation, the maturity table and cash-flow classification. Afterwards the reader can build the full schedule for a ten-year store lease and rebuild Dollar General's note from its disclosures.
parts: Is there a lease in this contract? The identified asset, the right to control and the components inside a rent cheque
How long and how much: the lease term, the payments that count, and the discount rate a retailer must invent
Finance or operating: the five tests and the two expense patterns that follow
The schedule: a ten-year store lease carried year by year through both statements, then remeasured when the option is exercised
Reading a lease note: Dollar General's maturity table, the weighted-average rate, and what the analyst does with it
worked_examples: Dollar General's fiscal 2024 10-K (year ended 31 January 2025): current operating lease liabilities of $1.46 billion and long-term of $9.76 billion, a 9.4-year weighted-average remaining term, a 4.5% weighted-average discount rate, $1.89 billion of operating lease cost and $1.59 billion of right-of-use assets obtained for new leases — reconstructing the liability from the maturity table

A ten-year store lease at $1.2 million a year with 2% escalators and a five-year renewal option, discounted at a 5.5% incremental borrowing rate: the liability, the ROU asset, the straight-line cost, and the year-six remeasurement when renewal becomes reasonably certain
Delta Air Lines' 2023 10-K: finance leases of aircraft beside operating leases of airport facilities — one note, two expense patterns, and the cash-flow classification of each

An incremental borrowing rate built from a company's secured borrowing curve on a stated date, rather than the unsecured yield the treasury desk quotes, and the effect of 100 basis points on the liability
sources: FASB ASC 842, Leases (ASU 2016-02 and amendments, incl. ASU 2018-11 and ASU 2021-09)
KPMG, Handbook: Leases (current edition)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Leases, lessor side, and the sale-leaseback
days.headline_hint: Big Lots sold four warehouses, kept every one, and booked a $463 million gain — the other side of the lease
days.focus: The lessor's book and the transaction that joins both sides. Lessor classification into sales-type, direct financing and operating; the net investment in the lease (lease receivable plus unguaranteed residual), selling profit recognised at commencement in a sales-type lease and deferred in a direct financing lease, the operating lessor's straight-line income with the asset still on its books, initial direct costs, variable payments and collectibility. Sale-leaseback under ASC 842-40: the ASC 606 test for whether a sale occurred, repurchase options, off-market terms, and the failed sale that is accounted for as a financing. Lease modifications, terminations, subleases and common-control arrangements. Afterwards the reader can account for both sides of the Big Lots transaction and see what a sale-leaseback does to leverage, earnings and cash flow.
parts: The lessor's three answers: sales-type, direct financing, operating — and what 'net investment in the lease' contains
Selling profit now or later: the sales-type lease as a sale with financing, and the direct financing lease as a loan
The operating lessor keeps the asset: straight-line income, depreciation and the net-lease REIT's income statement
Sale-leaseback: the ASC 606 sale test, repurchase options, off-market terms and the failed sale that is a loan
Modifications, terminations and subleases: when a new lease is created and when it is not
worked_examples: Big Lots' fiscal 2020 10-K (year ended 30 January 2021): the $725 million sale-leaseback of four distribution centres with affiliates of Oak Street (closed 16 June 2020), the $463.1 million gain on sale, the new operating leases — and the same deal re-run as a failed sale under a repurchase option
Air Lease Corporation's 2023 10-K: aircraft on operating leases — rental income, depreciation of flight equipment, lease incentives — against a sales-type lease of the same aircraft
Realty Income's 2023 10-K: straight-line rent receivable and the net-lease income statement, matched against the tenant's operating-lease cost from the same contract

A $2 million machine leased for five years at $460,000 a year with a $200,000 unguaranteed residual: the implicit rate, the sales-type entries, and the direct-financing entries when a third party guarantees the residual

ASU 2023-01, Leases — Common Control Arrangements

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Income taxes at depth: deferred taxes, valuation allowances and uncertain positions
days.headline_hint: Tesla's best quarter ever was a tax accounting entry — ASC 740 from the balance sheet up
days.focus: Year one's day 82 taught current versus deferred and effective versus statutory; this lesson takes ASC 740 to the bottom. The balance-sheet method: temporary differences, enacted rates, scheduling, and what a rate change does to an existing balance. The rate reconciliation and ASU 2023-09's disaggregated disclosures. The valuation allowance — more likely than not, the four sources of taxable income, cumulative losses as negative evidence, and the release. Uncertain tax positions under ASC 740-10: the recognition step, the measurement step (the largest amount with more than 50% cumulative probability), interest and penalties, the roll-forward. Outside basis differences and indefinite reinvestment, intraperiod allocation after ASU 2019-12, stock-compensation windfalls, NOL limitations, the GILTI policy election and Pillar Two as a period cost. Afterwards the reader can rebuild a rate reconciliation and judge whether a valuation-allowance release was supportable.
parts: Book versus tax: temporary differences, enacted rates and the balance-sheet method ASC 740 actually uses
The rate reconciliation: how 21% becomes something else, and what ASU 2023-09 now forces into the open
Will we ever use it? The valuation allowance, the four sources of taxable income and Tesla's release
Positions we might lose: the two-step test for uncertain tax benefits, and Microsoft's $28.9 billion notice
Earnings that never come home: outside basis differences, indefinite reinvestment and the one-time charges that end them
One number, several statements: intraperiod allocation, OCI, stock-compensation windfalls and the cash flow statement
worked_examples: Tesla's 2023 10-K: the release of $6.54 billion of valuation allowance on U.S. federal and state deferred tax assets (California excepted), the $5.9 billion one-time non-cash benefit in the fourth quarter, the $892 million of allowance retained, and the positive-and-negative-evidence reasoning in the note

Microsoft's fiscal 2024 10-K: the IRS Notices of Proposed Adjustment received September 2023 seeking $28.9 billion for tax years 2004–2013, the unrecognised tax benefits roll-forward, and the measurement step applied to a transfer-pricing position

Apple's fiscal 2024 10-K: the $10.2 billion net one-time charge after the Court of Justice of the EU upheld the 2016 State Aid decision — $15.8 billion payable to Ireland from escrow, offset by a $4.8 billion U.S. foreign tax credit and an $823 million decrease in unrecognised tax benefits

A three-year schedule for a $50 million machine depreciated straight-line for books and under MACRS for tax at a 21% rate: the deferred tax liability built, reversed, and repriced when the enacted rate changes

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Pensions and OPEB: the funded status, net periodic cost and the corridor
days.headline_hint: A promise made in 1985 is still moving Boeing's equity today — the actuarial accounts under ASC 715
days.focus: Defined benefit pensions and other postretirement benefits taught to the actuary's level of detail. The projected, accumulated and vested benefit obligations and why the discount rate is the whole argument; plan assets and the expected long-term return; the funded status on the balance sheet; the five components of net periodic pension cost and the one that is a smoothing device; the corridor and the alternative of immediate recognition; the pension line inside accumulated OCI; settlements, curtailments and special termination benefits; retiree medical under ASC 715-60 with the health-care cost trend; multiemployer plans and the withdrawal liability; presentation after ASU 2017-07. Afterwards the reader can rebuild a pension note from its disclosed components and estimate what a 50 basis point change in the discount rate does to the obligation and to equity.
parts: The promise as a liability: the PBO, the ABO, and why the discount rate is the whole argument
Plan assets and the expected return: what is real, what is assumed, and the gap that appears every year
Net periodic pension cost: five components, one of which is a smoothing device
The corridor, the alternative, and the pension line inside AOCI
Settlements, curtailments and buy-outs: how a company leaves a plan, and what the statements show
Retiree medical and multiemployer plans: OPEB under ASC 715-60, and the withdrawal liability that is not on the balance sheet
worked_examples: Boeing's 2023 10-K postretirement note: the projected benefit obligation, plan assets, funded status, the discount-rate and expected-return assumptions and the AOCI balances — rebuilding net periodic cost from the disclosed components

UPS's 2023 10-K: the mark-to-market policy that recognises actuarial gains and losses immediately each fourth quarter, set against corridor smoothing at Boeing — the same economics, two income statements

A two-year plan simulation: a $1 billion PBO, $800 million of assets, a 5.0% discount rate, a 6.5% expected return and a $60 million actuarial loss — the corridor test, the amortisation, and the sensitivity to a 50 basis point rate cut
IBM's 2023 10-K: non-operating retirement-related cost presented below operating income under ASU 2017-07, and the U.S. plan's shift to a fully funded, liability-matched bond portfolio

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Share-based compensation: grant-date fair value, attribution and the award that vests on a share price
days.headline_hint: Tesla's board gave its CEO a $2.3 billion option and the accountants expensed it before a single milestone was met — ASC 718 in full
days.focus: Year one's day 99 derived Black-Scholes and day 78 taught dilution; this lesson uses both to account for equity pay under ASC 718. Grant-date fair value and its inputs (expected term, volatility, dividends, the risk-free rate; RSUs at share price), attribution straight-line or graded, the forfeiture election, and the three kinds of condition — service, performance and market — with market conditions baked into fair value and performance conditions recognised when probable with a cumulative catch-up. Liability-classified awards remeasured each period, employee stock purchase plans, modifications of each type and their incremental fair value, nonemployee awards, and the tax accounting: the deferred tax asset on book expense and the windfall or shortfall through income tax expense. The treasury-stock method's use of unrecognised compensation is set up for the next lesson. Afterwards the reader can expense a real award schedule and reconcile the stock-based compensation line in a cash flow statement.
parts: What an option is worth on the day it is granted: the inputs, the expected term and why volatility is the fight
Spreading the cost: straight-line, graded vesting and the forfeiture election
Three kinds of condition: service, performance and market — and the one that is baked into fair value
Tesla's 2018 CEO award: twelve tranches, Monte Carlo, and the derived service period
Liabilities, ESPPs and modifications: awards that are remeasured, and awards that are repriced
Taxes and dilution: the deferred tax asset, the windfall, and what the SBC add-back in the cash flow statement means
worked_examples: Tesla's 2018 CEO Performance Award (granted 21 January 2018; about 20.3 million option shares in twelve tranches; grant-date fair value about $2.3 billion): market-capitalisation milestones as market conditions valued by Monte Carlo simulation, operational milestones as performance conditions recognised when probable, and the expense pattern in Tesla's 2018–2022 10-Ks

Amazon's 2023 10-K: $24.0 billion of stock-based compensation expense on restricted stock units, the vesting schedules disclosed, and the unrecognised compensation with its weighted-average remaining period

A 100,000-option grant with a $50 strike, four-year graded vesting, 35% volatility, a 4.2% risk-free rate and a six-year expected term: the Black-Scholes value, graded versus straight-line attribution, and a repricing to $30 in year two accounted for as a modification with incremental fair value

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Equity transactions and EPS: treasury stock, preferred, and the diluted share count
days.headline_hint: The denominator is a judgment — how a company decides how many shares it has
days.focus: Year one's day 78 taught issuance, buybacks and dilution as ideas; this lesson does the entries and the share counts. Preferred stock (cumulative, participating, redeemable — and the mezzanine under ASC 480-10-S99), treasury stock under the cost and par-value methods and retirement, stock dividends small and large, splits, property and liquidating dividends, warrants and rights, mandatorily redeemable instruments as liabilities under ASC 480, and convertible debt after ASU 2020-06. Then ASC 260 to the bottom: basic EPS with the weighted-average count and the preferred claim; diluted EPS by the treasury-stock method with unrecognised compensation as assumed proceeds, the if-converted method, contingently issuable shares, the antidilution ranking test, the two-class method for participating securities, and loss periods. Afterwards the reader can reproduce a company's EPS table and every decision inside its denominator.

Dividends that are not cash: stock dividends, splits, property dividends and what retained earnings absorbs

Diluted EPS: the treasury-stock method, if-converted, the ranking test and the two-class method
Three EPS tables read from filings: Alphabet's classes, Berkshire's A and B, and Strategy's convertibles

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Business combinations: the acquisition method from consideration to goodwill
days.headline_hint: Microsoft paid $75 billion for Activision and $51 billion of it has no name — the purchase price allocation, line by line
days.focus: Year one's day 86 said what happens when one company owns another; this lesson does the day-one accounting under ASC 805. Whether what was bought is a business (the ASU 2017-01 screen test) and why the answer changes goodwill, in-process R&D and transaction costs; identifying the acquirer and the acquisition date; measuring consideration — cash, shares at the closing price, contingent consideration at fair value with later remeasurement through income, replacement awards, settlement of pre-existing relationships. Recognising and measuring what was bought: inventory step-ups, plant, the identifiable intangibles (customer relationships, technology, trade names, IPR&D), contingencies, leases, deferred taxes on every step-up, and the noncontrolling interest at fair value. Goodwill as the residual, the bargain purchase, the measurement period, step acquisitions, pushdown accounting and the pro forma disclosures. Afterwards the reader can reconstruct an allocation and forecast the earnings hangover it creates.
parts: Business or asset? The screen test and why the answer changes the accounting
Who bought whom, and when: the acquirer, the acquisition date and the price in shares
What was paid: contingent consideration, replacement awards and the settlement of old relationships
What was bought: identifiable intangibles, the inventory step-up, deferred taxes on every step-up, and the NCI at fair value
The residual: goodwill, the bargain purchase, and the year-long measurement period

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Consolidation at depth: VIEs, eliminations, changes in ownership and the equity method
days.headline_hint: Control without ownership: the variable interest entity, and the eliminations that make one company out of many
days.focus: Year one's day 86 taught the idea of consolidation and minority interests; this lesson does the worksheet and the harder judgments under ASC 810. The two models in order — the variable interest model first (insufficient equity at risk, decision rights, the primary beneficiary's power and economics, reconsideration events, the disclosures for consolidated and nonconsolidated VIEs), then the voting model. Consolidation procedures in full: eliminating the investment against acquisition-date fair values, amortising the differential, intra-entity inventory and fixed-asset profits upstream and downstream, intercompany debt, the noncontrolling interest's share and the attribution of losses. Changes in ownership without loss of control as equity transactions, deconsolidation and the gain on the retained interest, and the equity method under ASC 323 with basis differences, impairment and losses beyond the investment. Afterwards the reader can build a two-years-after consolidation worksheet for a partially owned subsidiary and read a bank's VIE note.
parts: Two doors into consolidation: the variable interest model, then the voting model
Who is the primary beneficiary? Power, economics and JPMorgan's securitisation trusts
The worksheet: eliminating the investment, amortising the differential and the noncontrolling interest's share
Profits that never left the family: intra-entity inventory and fixed-asset sales, upstream and downstream
Buying more, selling some, losing control: equity transactions versus deconsolidation gains
One line for a company: the equity method, basis differences and Coca-Cola's bottlers

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Foreign currency: functional currency, remeasurement, translation and highly inflationary economies
days.headline_hint: The same peso loss lands in net income for one company and in OCI for another — the functional-currency decision under ASC 830
days.focus: Year one's day 129 taught exchange rates; this lesson taught what ASC 830 does with them. Foreign-currency transactions and the remeasurement of monetary items through income. The functional-currency indicators and why that single judgment decides the method: remeasurement under the temporal method (monetary items at current rates, nonmonetary at historical, the gain or loss in earnings) versus translation under the current-rate method (assets and liabilities at closing, income at average, equity at historical, the cumulative translation adjustment in OCI). The highly-inflationary rule — cumulative three-year inflation of roughly 100%, the practitioners' task-force list, Argentina since 1 July 2018 — and the switch to the parent's currency. Long-term intra-entity balances, the release of CTA on disposal or substantial liquidation, net-investment hedges in outline, and the disclosures. Afterwards the reader can translate and remeasure a subsidiary's trial balance and explain a CTA movement.
parts: A sale in euros: transaction gains and losses, and the balance-sheet items that move with the rate
Whose currency is it? The functional-currency indicators, and why the answer decides the method
Remeasurement: the temporal method, historical rates for inventory and plant, and the loss that hits earnings
Translation: the current-rate method, the cumulative translation adjustment, and what releases it
When money stops working: the highly-inflationary rule, Argentina, and Colgate's Latin America
worked_examples: Colgate-Palmolive's 2023 10-K: the currency-translation policy that remeasures highly-inflationary subsidiaries' non-monetary assets at historical rates and takes remeasurement through net income, applied to Argentina (highly inflationary under ASC 830 from 1 July 2018), beside Latin America's 13% net selling-price increases in the same filing

A subsidiary trial balance in euros (opening rate 1.05, average 1.08, closing 1.10, inventory bought at 1.07, plant at 0.95): translated under the current-rate method with the CTA derived, then remeasured under the temporal method with the gain or loss derived, and the two balance sheets compared

Apple's fiscal 2024 10-K: the foreign currency translation line inside other comprehensive income and the AOCI roll-forward, against the remeasurement gains and losses Microsoft reports within other income
Procter & Gamble's fiscal 2024 10-K: the exit from Argentina, the release of the accumulated translation adjustment into the loss on disposal, and the entries on the day the CTA leaves OCI

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: The statement of cash flows at depth: classification, reconstruction and the free-cash-flow bridge
days.headline_hint: Amazon publishes three free cash flows and none of them is the one you would compute — ASC 230 rebuilt from the balance sheet
days.focus: Year one's day 22 taught the three sections and why the statement is hard to fake; this lesson teaches how it is built and where it bends. The classification rules and the eight cases ASU 2016-15 had to settle (debt prepayment costs, contingent consideration payments, insurance proceeds, equity-method distributions, beneficial interests, the predominance principle), restricted cash after ASU 2016-18, and supplier finance programs under ASU 2022-04. The full indirect-method reconstruction from two balance sheets, an income statement and an acquisition — stripping acquired balances and the FX effect so the statement ties. Where the accruals hide: deferred taxes, stock compensation, pension contributions versus expense, operating and finance leases. Noncash investing and financing, interest and taxes paid, the direct-method reconciliation, and the analyst's adjustments — capitalised content and software, finance-lease principal, SBC. Afterwards the reader can rebuild a cash flow statement that ties and reconcile Amazon's three free-cash-flow measures.
parts: Operating, investing, financing — and the eight cases where the answer was not obvious
The reconstruction: from two balance sheets, an income statement and an acquisition to a cash flow statement that ties
Where the accruals hide: deferred taxes, stock compensation, pensions, leases and the working-capital lines
Amazon's three free cash flows and Netflix's content spend: what the statement does not classify for you
Supplier finance, restricted cash and the direct method: the disclosures that changed the statement in the 2020s
worked_examples: Amazon's 2023 10-K: operating cash flow of $84.9 billion, purchases of property and equipment of $52.7 billion less proceeds, free cash flow of $36.8 billion, the $24.0 billion stock-based compensation add-back, and the two further measures that subtract finance-lease and financing-obligation principal — reconciled line by line

A full indirect-method reconstruction for a company that made a $120 million acquisition during the year: stripping acquired working capital and PP&E from the balance-sheet deltas, isolating the FX effect, and tying to the change in cash and restricted cash

Netflix's 2023 10-K: about $13 billion of cash payments for content assets against $14.2 billion of content amortisation in the income statement, and the bridge from net income to operating cash flow that the difference creates
Boeing's 2023 10-K: the supplier finance program obligations disclosed under ASU 2022-04, and the classification of the payments that settle them
sources: FASB ASC 230, Statement of Cash Flows (incl. ASU 2016-15, Classification of Certain Cash Receipts and Cash Payments; ASU 2016-18, Restricted Cash; ASU 2022-04, Supplier Finance Programs)

Mulford & Comiskey, Creative Cash Flow Reporting: Uncovering Sustainable Financial Performance (Wiley, 2005)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: The back of the book: segments, contingencies, guarantees, subsequent events and related parties
days.headline_hint: 3M booked $16 billion of settlements before a dollar was paid, and Broadcom bought VMware three weeks after its year ended — the notes that carry the risk
days.focus: The notes a careful reader turns to first. Segment reporting under ASC 280: the management approach, the chief operating decision maker, operating segments, the aggregation criteria, the 10% and 75% tests, ASU 2023-07's significant segment expenses and the entity-wide disclosures. Contingencies under ASC 450: probable, reasonably possible and remote, the low end of a range, gain contingencies, discounting when timing is fixed, unasserted claims and the litigation accrual. Guarantees under ASC 460 at fair value, subsequent events under ASC 855 (recognised versus nonrecognised, the evaluation date for SEC filers, reissuance), related parties under ASC 850, risks and uncertainties, and the going-concern assessment. Afterwards the reader can apply the segment tests to a real company, judge a litigation accrual against its disclosed range and classify any post-year-end event.
parts: How a company is cut up for the reader: the CODM, operating segments, the 10% and 75% tests, and ASU 2023-07's expense disclosures
Probable, reasonably possible, remote: ASC 450 and the low end of the range
3M's PFAS and Combat Arms accruals: present value, insurance recoveries and the reasonably-possible range
After the balance sheet date: recognised and nonrecognised subsequent events, and Broadcom's Note 15
Guarantees, related parties and going concern: the notes that are read only when something is wrong
worked_examples: Amazon's 2024 10-K: North America, International and AWS as reportable segments, the significant segment expenses newly disclosed under ASU 2023-07, and the 10% and 75% tests applied to the disclosed figures

3M's 2023 10-K: the $10.3 billion accrual for the public water systems PFAS settlement measured at the pre-tax present value of payments over thirteen years, and the $6.0 billion Combat Arms earplug settlement ($5.0 billion in cash and $1.0 billion in stock, 2023–2029) — with the reasonably-possible-loss disclosure and the insurance-receivable question

Broadcom's fiscal 2023 10-K (year ended 29 October 2023, filed 14 December 2023): the VMware merger completed 22 November 2023 disclosed as a nonrecognised subsequent event in Note 15 — and what a recognised event would have looked like instead
Johnson & Johnson's 2023 10-K: the talc litigation accruals and the disclosed range, the related-party disclosures, and a parent's guarantee of a subsidiary's debt under ASC 460
sources: FASB ASC 280, Segment Reporting (incl. ASU 2023-07, Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures); ASC 450, Contingencies; ASC 460, Guarantees; ASC 855, Subsequent Events; ASC 850, Related Party Disclosures
SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin Topic 5.Y (Accounting and Disclosures Relating to Loss Contingencies)
3M Company, Form 10-K for fiscal 2023, the Commitments and Contingencies note
Broadcom Inc., Form 10-K for fiscal 2023, Note 15 (Subsequent Events)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Not-for-profit accounting: net assets with and without donor restrictions, contributions and the functional expense matrix
days.headline_hint: A hospital with no shareholders still has to explain where the money went — ASC 958 at Carnegie Mellon and UPMC
days.focus: The FASB framework for entities without owners. The four NFP statements; the two net-asset classes after ASU 2016-14 (with and without donor restrictions), board designations and underwater endowments. Contributions under ASC 958-605: unconditional versus conditional (the barrier and the right of return after ASU 2018-08), exchange transactions versus contributions, discounted promises to give, contributed services and gifts-in-kind after ASU 2020-07, and releases from restriction. Endowments under UPMIFA — and Pennsylvania's own non-UPMIFA statute — with spending policies; split-interest agreements; investment return presentation; the statement of functional expenses; the liquidity and availability disclosure; and healthcare NFPs under ASC 954, where patient service revenue runs through ASC 606 with implicit price concessions and a performance indicator. Afterwards the reader can read Carnegie Mellon's and UPMC's statements and tell donor-restricted from board-designated at a glance.
parts: No owners, two classes: net assets with and without donor restrictions, and the board's own designations
Is it a gift? Contributions versus exchanges, conditions versus restrictions, and the promise that is a receivable
The endowment: UPMIFA, Pennsylvania's own rule, the spending policy, and the fund that goes underwater
Where the money went: the statement of functional expenses, programme versus supporting, and the allocation the donor reads
A hospital's revenue: UPMC's patient service revenue, implicit price concessions and the performance indicator
worked_examples: Carnegie Mellon University's fiscal 2024 audited financial statements: about $5.9 billion of net assets at 30 June 2024, the $38.6 million of capital contributions released from donor restrictions, and the endowment's spending distribution under the university's policy

UPMC's audited consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024 (published March 2025): net patient service revenue with implicit price concessions under ASC 606, the excess of revenues over expenses as the performance indicator, and net assets by class

A $5 million pledge payable over five years, first conditional on matching funds and then unconditional: the discounted receivable, the release when the barrier is met, and the entries on the statement of financial position and the statement of activities
The American Red Cross's fiscal 2024 (30 June) statements: the statement of functional expenses matrix, gifts-in-kind presented under ASU 2020-07, and the liquidity and availability note
sources: FASB ASC 958, Not-for-Profit Entities (incl. ASU 2016-14, ASU 2018-08 and ASU 2020-07); ASC 954, Health Care Entities
AICPA Audit and Accounting Guide: Not-for-Profit Entities (current edition)
Uniform Prudent Management of Institutional Funds Act (2006) and Pennsylvania's separate endowment-spending statute, 15 Pa.C.S. §5548
Reck, Lowensohn & Neely, Accounting for Governmental & Nonprofit Entities, 19th ed. (McGraw Hill, 2021), chs. 13–16

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Governmental accounting: fund statements, modified accrual, and the ACFR reconciled
days.headline_hint: Pennsylvania keeps two sets of books by law, and both are right — GASB's fund and government-wide views, reconciled
days.focus: The capstone: a different framework, read end to end. Why governments count differently (accountability, the budget as law), the GASB and its hierarchy, and the two measurement focuses — current financial resources under modified accrual, economic resources under accrual. The eleven fund types across governmental, proprietary and fiduciary funds; the general fund's budgetary accounting with appropriations and encumbrances; revenue under modified accrual (measurable and available, the sixty-day property-tax rule, GASB 33's nonexchange categories); expenditures versus expenses; capital assets and long-term debt kept off the fund statements; GASB 54 fund balance classifications; the government-wide statement of net position and net-cost statement of activities; the two reconciliations; GASB 68 and 75 pension and OPEB liabilities, GASB 87 leases and GASB 96 SBITAs; component units, MD&A, the ACFR's three sections and GASB 103's coming changes. Afterwards the reader can read the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania's ACFR and the Chartiers Valley School District's audit, and reconcile fund balance to net position himself.
parts: Why governments count differently: accountability, the budget as law, and the two measurement focuses
The eleven funds: governmental, proprietary and fiduciary — and what each one's statements show
Modified accrual in practice: measurable and available, the sixty-day rule, encumbrances and the budgetary comparison
The government-wide view: net position, the statement of activities, and the pension liability that only appears there
The two reconciliations: from fund balance to net position, and from the change in fund balance to the change in net position
Reading the ACFR: the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania at 30 June 2024, and the Chartiers Valley School District audit
worked_examples: The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 2024 (jointly audited by the Department of the Auditor General and CliftonLarsonAllen): the General Fund balance sheet, the government-wide statement of net position with the net pension liability, and the reconciliation between them

Chartiers Valley School District's most recent annual independent audit (the district that serves Bridgeville): the General Fund's budget-to-actual schedule, the capital projects and debt service funds, GASB 68 amounts for PSERS, and fund balance by GASB 54 classification

A $40 million property-tax levy with $1.5 million collected between 61 and 120 days after year-end: fund revenue under the sixty-day rule, the deferred inflow of resources, and government-wide revenue — with journal entries in both views

A $12 million fire station financed by a bond issue: the capital projects fund, the debt service fund, the encumbrance on the construction contract, and the same asset and bond on the government-wide statement of net position
sources: GASB Codification of Governmental Accounting and Financial Reporting Standards; GASB Statements No. 34, 54, 68, 75, 87, 96 and 103
Government Finance Officers Association, Governmental Accounting, Auditing, and Financial Reporting (the 'Blue Book'), current edition
Reck, Lowensohn & Neely, Accounting for Governmental & Nonprofit Entities, 19th ed. (McGraw Hill, 2021), chs. 1–9
Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024 (Office of the Budget)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Ethics, independence and engagement acceptance
days.headline_hint: The opinion is only worth what the auditor refused to do for the client
days.focus: The AICPA Code of Professional Conduct's conceptual framework and independence rules (covered members, financial interests, loans, employment, nonattest services, fees), the SEC's Rule 2-01 of Regulation S-X and the PCAOB's Rules 3500T–3526 for issuer audits, and how those rules gate engagement acceptance and continuance under AU-C 210, AS 1000 and the firm's quality-management system (SQMS 1; PCAOB QC 1000, now effective December 15, 2026). Professional-exam level: the reader can test a fact pattern for an independence impairment, cite the section that decides it, and draft the acceptance memo and engagement letter for a first-year audit.
parts: Why independence is a market problem before it is an ethics problem
The Code's conceptual framework: threats, safeguards and the covered member
What the SEC and the PCAOB add for issuers: prohibited services, fees, rotation, cooling-off
Nonattest services, contingent fees, commissions and confidentiality — the lines firms actually cross
Accepting the engagement: preconditions, the predecessor, the letter and the quality system behind it
worked_examples: The SEC's June 28, 2022 order against Ernst & Young ($100 million; exam cheating and misleading the staff) and the 2019 KPMG order ($50 million; stolen PCAOB inspection data) mapped clause by clause to ET §1.400 acts discreditable, ET §1.100 integrity and objectivity, and PCAOB Rule 3500T

A covered-member test on Apple's auditor: an EY engagement partner, a tax manager on the team and an office-managing partner each holding AAPL in a retirement account, resolved under ET §1.240 and Rule 2-01(c)(1); then the five-year lead-partner rotation of Rule 2-01(c)(6) against the 'auditor since 2009' tenure line in EY's report in Apple's FY2024 10-K

Deloitte's fee table in Microsoft's 2025 proxy statement (audit, audit-related, tax, all other) tested against Rule 2-01(c)(4) prohibited non-audit services, the audit-committee pre-approval requirement of Rule 2-01(c)(7), and PCAOB Rule 3524's steps for pre-approving tax services

Drafting the AU-C 210 preconditions checklist, the predecessor inquiry (AU-C 210.11–.13 / AS 2610) and the engagement letter for a first-year audit of a private Pennsylvania manufacturer, with the AS 1000 responsibilities paragraph
sources: AICPA Code of Professional Conduct (2014 codification, as revised through 2025), ET §§0.300, 1.100, 1.200–1.297, 1.400, 1.510–1.520, 1.700
SEC Regulation S-X Rule 2-01, 17 CFR §210.2-01; Sarbanes-Oxley Act §§201–206
PCAOB Rules 3500T, 3501, 3520–3526; PCAOB AS 1000 (General Responsibilities of the Auditor) and QC 1000
AICPA AU-C 210 (Terms of Engagement) and SQMS No. 1; AU-C 220 (SAS 146)
