days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Risk assessment, materiality and planning
days.headline_hint: Every audit begins by deciding how wrong it is allowed to be
days.focus: The audit risk model as conditional probability, materiality and performance materiality computed from real benchmarks, the SAS 145 / AS 2110 risk-assessment procedures (understanding the entity, the inherent-risk spectrum, significant risks, the risk of material misstatement at the assertion level), fraud risk under AS 2401 / AU-C 240 and the presumption about revenue, and the audit plan and strategy that fall out of it. Professional-exam level: the reader can set materiality for a named company, rate its risks on the spectrum, and write the planned response by assertion.
parts: Audit risk is a product of three probabilities, and only one of them is yours
Materiality: the benchmark, the haircut and the number below which nothing gets posted
Understanding the entity: SAS 145's inherent-risk spectrum and what makes a risk 'significant'
Fraud: the triangle, the brainstorming, and why revenue is presumed guilty
From risks to a plan: the audit strategy, the timing of procedures and the assertion-level response
worked_examples: Materiality for Apple's FY2024 audit: income before taxes of $123.5 billion → 5% benchmark $6.2 billion overall, performance materiality at 75% ($4.6 billion), clearly-trivial threshold at 5% of overall ($310 million); then the same exercise on Rivian's FY2024 10-K (net loss $4.7 billion, revenue $4.97 billion) where a revenue or total-asset benchmark must replace earnings

The risk model with numbers: acceptable audit risk 5%, inherent risk assessed at 100% and control risk at 50% → detection risk 10%, and how that 10% becomes the confidence factor for the sample sizes of day 4 (24 of 40)

A fraud brainstorming on Kraft Heinz's FY2018 supplier-rebate misconduct (10-K filed June 7, 2019; SEC press release 2021-174): incentive, opportunity and rationalisation, the assertions affected, and the AS 2401 procedures the risk demands

Rating Spirit AeroSystems' FY2024 forward-loss estimates on the B787, B767, A350 and A220 programs (operating loss $1.79 billion) on the SAS 145 spectrum of complexity, subjectivity and uncertainty, and naming the significant risks
sources: PCAOB AS 2101 (Audit Planning), AS 2105 (Consideration of Materiality), AS 2110 (Identifying and Assessing Risks of Material Misstatement), AS 2401 (Consideration of Fraud)
AICPA AU-C 300, 315 (as amended by SAS 145), 320 and 240
Arens, Elder, Beasley & Hogan, Auditing and Assurance Services (18th ed., Pearson), chapters on materiality, risk and fraud
Kraft Heinz Co., Form 10-K for fiscal 2018 (filed 2019-06-07), Item 9A; Spirit AeroSystems Holdings, Form 10-K for fiscal 2024
days.exam_map: AUD Area II – Assessing Risk and Developing a Planned Response (planning, materiality, risk assessment, fraud)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Internal control, COSO and the ICFR audit
days.headline_hint: A material weakness is a sentence about probability, not a confession
days.focus: The COSO 2013 framework (five components, seventeen principles), the auditor's understanding and testing of controls under AS 2110 / AU-C 315, the integrated audit of internal control over financial reporting under AS 2201 (top-down scoping, entity-level controls, IT general controls, walkthroughs, tests of design and operating effectiveness), and the deficiency ladder — deficiency, significant deficiency, material weakness — with the language of Item 9A and Item 4.01. Professional-exam level: the reader can classify a deficiency with the AS 2201 indicators and read a real adverse ICFR opinion.
parts: Control is a feedback loop: COSO's five components and the seventeen things a control system must do
Getting from the top down: entity-level controls, significant accounts and where the audit actually looks
IT general controls and automated controls: why one test can cover a million transactions
Testing design and testing operation: walkthroughs, sample sizes and the frequency table
The deficiency ladder and what Item 9A has to say when a rung is missed
When the auditor walks: Item 4.01, the resignation letter and what it signals
worked_examples: Kraft Heinz FY2018 Item 9A parsed against COSO: the risk-assessment material weakness (principles 6–9) and the supplier-contracts control failure (principles 10–12), with PwC's adverse opinion on ICFR alongside its unqualified opinion on the statements

Top-down scoping of Walmart's FY2025 integrated audit (revenues $681 billion, thousands of locations): entity-level controls, the significant-account and location decisions, and AS 2201's 'reasonable possibility of a material misstatement' test applied to three hypothetical deficiencies using the .62–.70 indicators

Super Micro Computer: EY's October 24, 2024 resignation reported on Form 8-K Item 4.01 (filed October 30, 2024) — what Item 304 of Regulation S-K forces the company and the auditor to say, and the material weaknesses later disclosed in the delayed fiscal-2024 10-K

An ITGC walkthrough of a change-management control over an ERP system: the design-and-implementation test, then a sample of 25 for a control operating many times a day and 2 for a quarterly control, following the AICPA's frequency-based sample-size guidance
sources: COSO, Internal Control — Integrated Framework (2013), Framework and Appendices
PCAOB AS 2201 (An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with an Audit of Financial Statements) and AS 2110 ¶¶ .18–.40
AICPA AU-C 315 (SAS 145) and AU-C 265 (Communicating Internal Control Related Matters)
SEC Regulation S-K Items 307, 308 and 304; Form 8-K Item 4.01; Kraft Heinz Co. Form 10-K for fiscal 2018, Item 9A
days.exam_map: AUD Area II – Assessing Risk and Developing a Planned Response (control environment, IT general controls and entity-level controls; COSO; ICFR)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Evidence, sampling and the work of others
days.headline_hint: How much proof is enough, and who is allowed to supply it
days.focus: Sufficiency and appropriateness of evidence under AS 1105 / AU-C 500 (SAS 142), the reliability hierarchy, external confirmations under the revised AS 2310 (effective for fiscal years ending on or after June 15, 2025), analytical procedures under AS 2305 / AU-C 520, audit sampling under AS 2315 / AU-C 530 done with real arithmetic (attribute sampling, monetary-unit sampling, projection and the upper misstatement limit), and reliance on others — auditor-engaged and company specialists (AS 1210, AS 1105 Appendix A, AU-C 620), internal auditors (AS 2605, AU-C 610), service organizations (AS 2601, AU-C 402) and component auditors (AS 1206, AU-C 600 as revised by SAS 149). Professional-exam level with the statistics carried through.
parts: Evidence has a hierarchy, and the auditor's own eyes sit at the top
Confirmations after the 2023 rewrite: cash, receivables, intermediaries and the non-response
Attribute sampling: deviation rates, confidence and the table that sets the sample
Monetary-unit sampling: the interval, the tainting and the upper limit
Analytical procedures: expectations precise enough to catch something
Borrowed evidence: specialists, internal audit, service organizations and component auditors
worked_examples: Monetary-unit sampling on Tesla's net accounts receivable of about $4.42 billion at December 31, 2024 (per the FY2024 10-K): tolerable misstatement $110 million, expected $20 million, 95% confidence (reliability factor 3.0, expansion factor 1.6) → sample size ≈ 3.0 × 4,420 / (110 − 32) ≈ 170 and a $26 million sampling interval; a $3 million item confirmed at $2.985 million gives a 0.5% tainting, projected and added to the basic precision to reach the upper misstatement limit

Attribute sampling of a purchase-approval control: tolerable deviation rate 5%, expected 1%, 95% confidence → 93 items from the AICPA table; one deviation found leaves the achieved upper limit at the tolerable rate, two found (≈6.6%) means the control cannot be relied on and control risk is reassessed

A confirmation program under the revised AS 2310: bank confirmation through a designated intermediary, positive confirmations for the 40 largest receivables and negative confirmations for 3,400 small balances, and the alternative procedures (subsequent cash receipts, shipping documents) that the standard now requires for non-responses

Reliance on a SOC 1 Type 2 report from a payroll processor under AS 2601 / AU-C 402: the complementary user-entity controls mapped to the client's own controls, the bridge-letter gap, and the AS 1210 evaluation of an actuary's assumptions on a defined-benefit obligation
sources: PCAOB AS 1105 (Audit Evidence) with Appendix A, AS 2310 (The Auditor's Use of Confirmation, 2023), AS 2315 (Audit Sampling), AS 2305, AS 1210, AS 2605, AS 2601, AS 1206
AICPA Audit Guide: Audit Sampling (2019 edition), including the attribute and MUS tables
Tesla, Inc., Form 10-K for fiscal 2024, consolidated balance sheet
days.exam_map: AUD Area III – Performing Further Procedures and Obtaining Evidence (sufficient appropriate evidence, sampling, external confirmations, using the work of others)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Substantive procedures by cycle, estimates and completing the audit
days.headline_hint: The audit is a set of questions asked of each account until it stops answering
days.focus: Substantive testing organised by transaction cycle — revenue and receivables (including ASC 606 judgments and cutoff), purchases and payables (search for unrecorded liabilities), inventory (observation, test counts, NRV), cash (bank reconciliations, kiting), property and leases, payroll, investments and fair value, debt and equity — each mapped to assertions; auditing accounting estimates under AS 2501 / AU-C 540 (SAS 143) with method, assumptions and data; and completion: going concern (AS 2415 / AU-C 570), subsequent events, litigation letters, management representations, evaluating misstatements and documentation. Professional-exam level: the reader can write the substantive program for a cycle and evaluate a real estimate.
parts: Assertions are the grammar: what every substantive procedure is really testing
Revenue and receivables: cutoff, side agreements and the five-step model under audit
Purchases, payables, inventory and cash: the search for what is missing
Property, leases, debt, equity and investments: agreeing the balance to the world outside
Estimates: the method, the assumptions, the data — and the auditor's own point estimate
Finishing: going concern, subsequent events, the lawyer's letter, the representation letter and the schedule of what was left unfixed
worked_examples: Revenue procedures behind Deloitte's revenue-recognition CAM on Microsoft's FY2025 10-K: testing stand-alone selling prices in multi-element commercial agreements, contract modifications, and cutoff around June 30 — the specific evidence for occurrence, accuracy and cutoff

A December 31 year-end search for unrecorded liabilities from subsequent disbursements through the report date, an inventory observation with test counts reconciled to the final listing and an NRV write-down, and a kiting test built from the interbank transfer schedule

Auditing Apple's $22.0 billion of gross unrecognized tax benefits at September 28, 2024 under AS 2501: evaluating the two-step ASC 740-10 method, the assumptions on settlement, and the data behind the reserve; then a going-concern evaluation of Spirit AeroSystems' FY2024 position (gross loss $1.37 billion) against management's plans under ASC 205-40 and AS 2415

Completion package: the AS 2505 legal-letter request under the ABA treaty, the AS 2805 representation letter, Type I versus Type II subsequent events under AS 2801 for an event dated after the balance sheet, and a schedule of unadjusted misstatements evaluated against day 2's materiality under AS 2810
sources: PCAOB AS 2501 (Auditing Accounting Estimates, Including Fair Value Measurements), AS 2415, AS 2505, AS 2801, AS 2805, AS 2810, AS 1215
Louwers, Blay, Sinason, Strawser & Thibodeau, Auditing & Assurance Services (9th ed., McGraw Hill), cycle chapters
Apple Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2024 (income taxes note); Microsoft Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 (auditor's report)
days.exam_map: AUD Area III – Performing Further Procedures and Obtaining Evidence (substantive procedures by cycle, accounting estimates, subsequent events, going concern, written representations)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Audit reports, critical audit matters and modifications
days.headline_hint: Read the auditor's report as a legal document — every clause was fought over
days.focus: The PCAOB report under AS 3101 (opinion first, basis, critical audit matters, tenure) and the AICPA report under AU-C 700 (SAS 134) with key audit matters, the integrated ICFR opinion under AS 2201, modifications under AS 3105 / AU-C 705 (qualified, adverse, disclaimer, and the basis paragraphs), explanatory and emphasis-of-matter paragraphs (going concern, consistency under AS 2820, other information under AU-C 720), comparatives and predecessor reports, and special-purpose and single-statement reports (AU-C 800–805). Professional-exam level: the reader can parse a real report sentence by sentence, say why a CAM was a CAM, and draft each modified opinion.
parts: The unqualified report, line by line: what each sentence promises and what it withholds
Critical audit matters: the test that selects them and the paragraph that explains them
Two opinions in one filing: the integrated ICFR report and the adverse case
When the opinion bends: scope limitations, GAAP departures, pervasiveness and the three modifications
Paragraphs that warn without modifying: going concern, consistency, emphasis and other information
Comparatives, predecessors, dual dating and the reports that are not on a full set of statements
worked_examples: EY's report on Apple's FY2024 10-K parsed clause by clause against AS 3101: the opinion paragraph, the basis paragraph, the CAM on uncertain tax positions (why it met the .11 definition; how the audit addressed it) and the 'auditor since 2009' tenure line

Deloitte's two CAMs on Microsoft FY2025 — revenue recognition and uncertain tax positions — read against the procedures of day 5, and what the 'how the CAM was addressed' language reveals about the audit that is otherwise invisible

The substantial-doubt paragraph in EY's report on Spirit AeroSystems' FY2024 10-K under AS 2415 and AS 3101, set beside PwC's adverse ICFR opinion on Kraft Heinz FY2018 as the model of the AS 2201 ¶ 90 language

A modification decision tree under AS 3105 / AU-C 705: an inventory observation that could not be performed (qualified or disclaimer by pervasiveness), a lease misclassified under ASC 842 (qualified or adverse), each with its basis paragraph drafted, and a comparative report where the predecessor's opinion is reissued
sources: PCAOB AS 3101 (The Auditor's Report on an Audit of Financial Statements When the Auditor Expresses an Unqualified Opinion), AS 3105, AS 2201 ¶¶ 85–98, AS 2415, AS 2820

Apple Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2024; Microsoft Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal 2025; Spirit AeroSystems Holdings Form 10-K for fiscal 2024; Kraft Heinz Co. Form 10-K for fiscal 2018 — each auditor's report as filed
PCAOB Staff Guidance, Implementation of Critical Audit Matters (2019–2020)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: SOC engagements, attestation, reviews and compilations
days.headline_hint: There are five levels of assurance and most of the world runs on the lower three
days.focus: The attestation family under SSAE 18–23 (AT-C 105, 205, 210, 215, 305, 320): examinations, reviews and agreed-upon procedures; SOC 1 reports on controls at a service organization (Type 1 versus Type 2, carve-out versus inclusive, complementary user-entity controls) and SOC 2 reports against the Trust Services Criteria (TSP section 100, 2017 with 2022 points of focus); SSARS engagements under AR-C 60/70/80/90 (preparation, compilation, review) and interim reviews of issuers under AS 4105 / AU-C 930. Professional-exam level: the reader can read a SOC report as a user auditor, write a review's analytical expectations, and draft each report's exact language.
parts: The ladder of assurance: examination, review, agreed-upon procedures, compilation, preparation
SOC 1: the service auditor's opinion, the tests table and the controls the user must supply
SOC 2 and the Trust Services Criteria: security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy
Reviews and compilations under SSARS: limited assurance, no assurance, and the reports that say so
Agreed-upon procedures, prospective information and the interim review of a public company
worked_examples: A SOC 1 Type 2 report from a payroll processor, read with the AICPA's illustrative AT-C 320 report: control objectives, tests and results, an exception in the input-change control, the carved-out data-center subservice organization, and the complementary user-entity controls a user auditor must test at the client

SOC 2 against TSP 100 for a cloud provider (AWS's own SOC 2 is distributed under NDA through AWS Artifact; the lesson works the public criteria CC6.1–CC6.8 on logical access): what a Type 2 opinion covers, the points of focus, and why a SOC 2 cannot be used to reduce control risk in a financial-statement audit the way a SOC 1 can

A review under AR-C 90 of a private distributor: gross-margin and days-sales expectations with investigation thresholds, the inquiries of management, the limited-assurance report text, versus the AR-C 80 compilation report (no assurance) and an AR-C 70 preparation engagement with its legend

An agreed-upon-procedures engagement under AT-C 215 (SSAE 19) on a franchisor's royalty computation, and Apple's Q1 FY2025 Form 10-Q reviewed under AS 4105 — what 'we are not aware of any material modifications' does and does not assert
sources: AICPA AT-C sections 105, 205, 210, 215, 305 and 320 (SSAE Nos. 18, 19, 21, 22 and 23)

AICPA, SOC 1 Guide: Reporting on an Examination of Controls at a Service Organization Relevant to User Entities' Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (2022) and SOC 2 Guide (2022); TSP section 100 (2017, with 2022 revised points of focus)
AICPA AR-C sections 60, 70, 80 and 90 (SSARS Nos. 21–26)
PCAOB AS 4105 (Reviews of Interim Financial Information); AICPA AU-C 930

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Individual income tax I: gross income, adjustments and deductions
days.headline_hint: Form 1040 is a funnel, and the whole Code is written in the order the numbers fall through it
days.focus: The individual tax formula from §61 gross income through exclusions (§§101–139), above-the-line adjustments (§62), the standard deduction versus itemized deductions (§§163(h), 164 with the OBBBA SALT cap, 165, 170, 213, and §68's absence), filing status and dependents (§§1, 2, 152), and the tax computed on the current year's brackets, with Pennsylvania's flat 3.07% and local earned-income tax alongside. Professional-exam level: the reader can prepare a complete 2026-rules return by hand and defend each line with the section that governs it. Figures are stated for tax year 2026 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32) and restated by the run for the latest year the IRS has published.
parts: Gross income means everything, unless a section says otherwise
The exclusions: what Congress decided not to count, and the ones people get wrong
Above the line: adjustments, phase-outs and why AGI is the number everything else keys off
Standard or itemized: the SALT cap, mortgage interest, charity and medical after the 2025 Act
Filing status, dependents and the marriage penalty, computed on the actual brackets
worked_examples: A 2026 joint return for a couple in Allegheny County: $185,000 wages, $12,000 qualified dividends, $9,800 of state and local taxes (under the $40,400 SALT cap), $14,200 mortgage interest, $3,000 charity → itemized $27,000 loses to the $32,200 standard deduction; taxable income $164,800; ordinary tax $23,040 on the 10/12/22% brackets ($24,800 / $100,800 / $211,400 breakpoints) plus $1,800 on the dividends at 15%; Pennsylvania's 3.07% and the local earned-income tax on top

Exclusions on real fact patterns: §101 life-insurance proceeds, §102 gifts and inheritances, §104 physical-injury damages versus taxable punitive awards, §108 cancellation-of-debt income and the insolvency exception, and the OBBBA deductions for qualified tips (up to $25,000) and overtime pay on a server's 2026 Form W-2

Adjustments with phase-outs: a traditional IRA deduction for an active participant against the 2026 AGI phase-out ranges (Notice 2025-67), student-loan interest, the HSA limits ($4,400 self-only / $8,750 family for 2026), and half of self-employment tax; then the 7.5%-of-AGI medical floor

Dependents and status: the qualifying-child and qualifying-relative tests of §152 with the 2026 gross-income limit, head-of-household for a divorced parent, and the marriage bonus/penalty computed by running two single returns against one joint return on the 2026 brackets
sources: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (2026 inflation adjustments); IRS Publication 17 and the Form 1040 instructions for the run year
Bittker, McMahon & Zelenak, Federal Income Taxation of Individuals (4th ed., Thomson Reuters), updated
Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, PA-40 instructions; Act 32 local earned-income tax
days.exam_map: REG Area IV – Federal Taxation of Individuals (gross income, adjustments, deductions, filing status)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Individual income tax II: credits, AMT, NIIT and the qualified business income deduction
days.headline_hint: The second tax system nobody plans for, and the credits that quietly set your marginal rate
days.focus: Everything that happens after taxable income: the ordering of capital-gain and qualified-dividend rates (§1(h)) with the 0/15/20% stacking, the alternative minimum tax (§§55–59, Form 6251) with the OBBBA exemption and phase-out, the 3.8% net investment income tax (§1411) and the 0.9% additional Medicare tax, nonrefundable and refundable credits (child, earned income, education, dependent care, premium, saver's) with their phase-outs, the §199A qualified business income deduction at the individual level, and estimated tax and the §6654 penalty. Professional-exam level: the reader can compute AMT on an ISO exercise and the true marginal rate inside a credit phase-out. Figures for 2026 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32), restated by the run.
parts: Preferential rates are a stack, not a bracket: how gains sit on top of ordinary income
The alternative minimum tax from the ground up: adjustments, preferences, exemption, phase-out and the credit that follows you
Surtaxes on investment income and wages: §1411 and the additional Medicare tax
Credits: refundable, nonrefundable, and the phase-outs that create marginal rates the tables never show
Section 199A at the individual level: the 20% deduction and its ceilings
Paying as you go: withholding, estimated tax, safe harbors and the penalty
worked_examples: AMT on an incentive-stock-option exercise: 10,000 options at a $15 strike when the stock is at $65 → a $500,000 preference; regular taxable income $250,000 (joint) → AMTI $750,000; the 2026 exemption of $140,200 survives intact below the $1,000,000 phase-out threshold → AMT base $609,800; 26% to $244,500 and 28% above → tentative minimum tax $165,854 against regular tax of $45,196 → AMT of $120,658 and a §53 minimum-tax credit carried forward

Rate stacking: $60,000 of ordinary income and $70,000 of long-term gain on a 2026 joint return — the 0% bracket to $98,900 absorbs part of the gain, the rest is taxed at 15%; then the 3.8% NIIT above $250,000 of MAGI and the 0.9% additional Medicare tax on wages above $250,000 (both thresholds unindexed)

Credits with phase-outs: the $2,200 child tax credit phasing out above $400,000 (joint), the 2026 EITC maximum of $8,231 for three children with its phase-in and phase-out slopes turned into marginal rates, the American Opportunity credit ($2,500, 40% refundable) against the Lifetime Learning credit, and the premium tax credit reconciliation on Form 8962

§199A for a Pennsylvania sole proprietor: $180,000 of QBI with $220,000 of joint taxable income (below the 2026 threshold) → the 20% deduction capped at 20% of taxable income less net capital gain; then the same business above the threshold where the W-2 wage / UBIA limit and the specified-service phase-in bite; estimated-tax safe harbors at 100% and 110% of prior-year tax
sources: Rev. Proc. 2025-32; IRS Forms 6251, 8960, 8812, 8995-A and instructions for the run year
Joint Committee on Taxation, General Explanation of P.L. 119-21 (when published) and JCX estimates of the 2025 Act
Bittker, McMahon & Zelenak, Federal Income Taxation of Individuals (4th ed.), chapters on AMT and credits
days.exam_map: REG Area IV – Federal Taxation of Individuals (credits, AMT, NIIT, qualified business income, estimated tax)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Property transactions: basis, cost recovery, recapture and nonrecognition
days.headline_hint: Basis is memory: every dollar that was ever taxed or deducted is written into the asset
days.focus: Realized versus recognized gain under §1001, basis rules (cost, §1015 gifts with dual basis, §1014 inheritances, §1091 wash sales, §267 related parties, stock splits and specific identification), MACRS, §179 and bonus depreciation as they set adjusted basis, the character machine — §1221 capital assets, §1231 with its five-year lookback, §1245 and §1250 recapture and the 25% unrecaptured §1250 gain — and the nonrecognition provisions: §1031 like-kind exchanges with boot and liabilities, §121 residences, §1033 involuntary conversions and §453 installment sales. Professional-exam level: the reader can compute the whole chain from purchase to disposal with real tables and the current-year limits.
parts: Realized, recognized, and the difference between them
Basis: where it comes from and how gifts, deaths, splits and wash sales rewrite it
Cost recovery as tax policy: MACRS tables, §179 and 100% bonus after the 2025 Act
Character: §1221, §1231's hotchpot and lookback, and the recapture sections that claw ordinary income back
Like-kind exchanges: boot, liabilities and the basis of what you get
Homes, disasters and installments: §121, §1033 and §453
worked_examples: A §1031 exchange with liabilities: a warehouse worth $2,400,000 (adjusted basis $900,000, $800,000 mortgage assumed by the buyer) exchanged for a $2,600,000 building carrying a $1,100,000 mortgage plus $100,000 cash paid — realized gain $1,500,000, no net boot received, recognized gain zero, and a §1031(d) basis of $1,300,000 in the replacement property (the deferred $1,500,000 sits inside it)

A $1,200,000 nonresidential building placed in service March 2019 (39-year straight-line, mid-month, Rev. Proc. 87-57 tables) sold in 2026: accumulated depreciation, unrecaptured §1250 gain taxed at 25%, §1231 netting with the lookback; and a 7-year machine expensed under §179 (2026 limit $2,560,000, phase-out from $4,090,000) or 100% bonus, fully recaptured as ordinary income under §1245 on sale

Basis on real securities: Apple shares received by gift (donor basis $12, value $230 — the §1015 dual-basis rule when the gift is later sold at a loss), shares inherited at the §1014 date-of-death value, a §1091 wash sale on Tesla stock sold at a loss and repurchased within 30 days with the disallowed loss added to basis, and specific identification versus average cost on a mutual fund

§121 on a Bridgeville home sold at a $420,000 gain by a married couple: the $500,000 exclusion, the two-of-five-year ownership and use tests, a reduced exclusion for a job-related move, and the recapture of home-office depreciation; then a §453 installment sale of land with the gross-profit percentage applied to each year's collections and the §453A interest charge above the threshold
sources: Rev. Proc. 87-57 (MACRS tables); IRS Publication 946 (How to Depreciate Property) and Publication 544 (Sales and Other Dispositions of Assets) for the run year
Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (§179 limits for 2026); P.L. 119-21 §70301 (permanent 100% bonus depreciation)
Bittker & Lokken, Federal Taxation of Income, Estates and Gifts (Thomson Reuters), chapters on basis and nonrecognition
days.exam_map: REG Area III – Federal Taxation of Property Transactions (basis, cost recovery, §1231/§1245/§1250, nontaxable dispositions)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: C corporations: formation, earnings and profits, distributions, liquidations and losses
days.headline_hint: The corporate tax is a second layer with its own memory, and E&P is the ledger it keeps
days.focus: Subchapter C from birth to death: §351 formation with boot, services and liabilities (§357), §358 and §362 basis; the corporate tax base at the 21% rate with the dividends-received deduction, the 10% charitable limit, capital-loss carryovers and the §172 NOL 80% limitation with §382 after an ownership change; earnings and profits under §312 and the §301/§316 characterization of distributions; §302 redemptions versus dividends; complete liquidations under §§331/336 and parent-subsidiary liquidations under §§332/337; the accumulated-earnings and personal-holding-company penalties; the 15% corporate alternative minimum tax on large filers; §1202 qualified small business stock after the 2025 Act; and the Schedule M-1/M-3 book-tax bridge back to the day-82 deferred-tax accounts. Professional-exam level.
parts: Forming the corporation without triggering tax: §351, control, boot and the liability trap
The corporate return: rate, dividends-received deduction, charitable limit and the losses that carry
Earnings and profits: the account that decides whether a distribution is a dividend
Redemptions: when giving back shares is a sale and when it is a dividend
Liquidations and the double tax paid at the exit, and the subsidiary exception
Penalties and shelters: accumulated earnings, personal holding companies, CAMT and §1202
worked_examples: A §351 formation: three shareholders contribute $300,000 cash, equipment (basis $50,000, value $200,000, subject to a $60,000 loan) and $50,000 of services for stock — the 80% control test, §357(c) gain where liabilities exceed basis, each shareholder's §358 basis and the corporation's §362 basis, and the service shareholder's ordinary income

Distributions against E&P: current E&P of −$40,000 and accumulated E&P of $100,000 with a $150,000 distribution — the §316 ordering, the dividend layer, the §301(c)(2) return of capital and the §301(c)(3) gain; then a §302(b)(2) substantially-disproportionate redemption tested at the 80% and 50% marks against the §302(b)(1) 'not essentially equivalent' standard

NOLs on a real balance sheet: Rivian's FY2024 10-K reports $4,621 million of deferred tax assets for NOL and credit carryforwards under a $6,228 million valuation allowance — apply the §172(a)(2) 80%-of-taxable-income limit to a hypothetical profitable year, then the §382 annual limitation (equity value × the long-term tax-exempt rate for the month of change) after an ownership change

A 2026 Form 1120 book-to-tax reconciliation: 21% under §11, a 50% DRD on a sub-20% holding, the 10% charitable ceiling, a capital-loss carryback, and the CAMT screen (average adjusted financial-statement income above $1 billion at 15%); a §1202 issuance in 2026 under the OBBBA tiers (50/75/100% exclusion at three, four and five years, $15 million cap)
sources: IRS Form 1120 and Schedule M-3 instructions for the run year; Rivian Automotive, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2024 (income taxes note)
Bittker & Eustice, Federal Income Taxation of Corporations and Shareholders (7th ed., Thomson Reuters), updated
P.L. 119-21 §70431 (§1202 changes); Rev. Rul. 2025 series long-term tax-exempt rates for §382
days.exam_map: REG Area V – Federal Taxation of Entities (C corporations)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: S corporations and partnerships: pass-through mechanics, basis and distributions
days.headline_hint: The entity pays nothing, so every dollar has to find an owner — and a basis to land in
days.focus: Subchapter S: eligibility and the §1362 election, separately stated items, the §1367 basis ordering rules for stock and debt basis, the §1368 distribution tiers with and without earnings and profits, the accumulated adjustments account, built-in gains under §1374, and reasonable compensation. Subchapter K: §721 formation, capital accounts under §704(b) and substantial economic effect, §704(c) built-in gain, §752 liability shares and outside basis, guaranteed payments, §731 distributions, §751 hot assets on a sale, the §754 election with §743(b) and §734(b) adjustments, and §736 payments to a retiring partner. The loss-limitation gauntlet in order — basis, at-risk, passive, excess business loss — and self-employment tax. Professional-exam level with the K-1 in hand.
parts: Choosing pass-through: what an S election buys, what it forbids and how it is lost
The shareholder's basis: the §1367 ordering rules and why distributions can become gain
Forming and allocating a partnership: capital accounts, substantial economic effect and §704(c)
Liabilities and outside basis: §752 and the debt that lets losses through
Distributions, hot assets and the §754 step-up: leaving a partnership without a surprise
The four gates every loss passes through, and who pays self-employment tax
worked_examples: An S shareholder's basis rollforward under §1367: opening stock basis $40,000, ordinary income $30,000, tax-exempt interest $2,000, a $55,000 distribution, $1,000 of nondeductible expenses and a $20,000 ordinary loss — ordering, the distribution in excess of basis taxed as §1368 capital gain, loss suspended for want of basis, debt-basis reduction and restoration; reasonable compensation with Watson v. Commissioner (8th Cir. 2012) as the benchmark

Partnership formation and §704(c): A contributes land (basis $100,000, value $400,000), B contributes $400,000 cash; the land is sold for $460,000 — the traditional method sends the $300,000 built-in gain to A and splits the $60,000 of post-contribution gain; then each partner's §752 share of a $600,000 recourse loan and the resulting outside basis

Selling an interest with hot assets: unrealized receivables and appreciated inventory carve ordinary income out of the capital gain under §751; the buyer's §754 election and §743(b) basis adjustment — using the Schedule K-1 line structure and the §754 disclosure in Enterprise Products Partners L.P.'s 2024 Form 10-K (a publicly traded partnership) as the real template

Loss limitations in sequence: basis (§1366(d) / §704(d)), at-risk (§465), passive activity (§469, with the $25,000 rental allowance phasing out from $100,000 to $150,000 of AGI) and the §461(l) excess-business-loss threshold for 2026 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32); then §1402 self-employment tax on a general partner's distributive share versus an S shareholder's salary

McKee, Nelson & Whitmire, Federal Taxation of Partnerships and Partners (4th ed., Thomson Reuters); Eustice, Kuntz & Bogdanski, Federal Income Taxation of S Corporations
Watson v. Commissioner, 668 F.3d 1008 (8th Cir. 2012)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Estate, gift and generation-skipping transfer tax, and the income taxation of trusts
days.headline_hint: The unified credit is a lifetime account, and every gift is a withdrawal from it
days.focus: The transfer-tax system as one integrated regime: taxable gifts under §§2501–2524 (annual exclusion, gift-splitting, marital and charitable deductions, §2503(e) tuition and medical payments), the gross estate under §§2031–2046 (retained interests under §2036, life insurance under §2042, joint property, powers of appointment), the estate-tax computation of §2001 with the unified credit on the current basic exclusion and portability of the deceased spousal unused exclusion, the generation-skipping transfer tax and exemption allocation, §1014 basis at death versus §1015 carryover, and the income taxation of estates and trusts (distributable net income, the distribution deduction, simple versus complex trusts, grantor trusts). Professional-exam level; figures for 2026 restated by the run.
parts: One tax, two events: how gifts and estates share a single lifetime exclusion
Taxable gifts: the annual exclusion, splitting, and the transfers that are not gifts at all
The gross estate: what death pulls back in — retained strings, insurance, joint property and powers
Computing the estate tax and porting what is left of the exclusion to the survivor
Skipping a generation: the GST tax, the exemption and the allocation decision
Trusts as taxpayers: DNI, the distribution deduction and the compressed brackets
worked_examples: A 2026 estate: gross estate $22,000,000 (a Bridgeville house, an IRA, a brokerage account and $2,000,000 of life insurance included under §2042), a $5,000,000 marital deduction and $500,000 of debts and expenses → taxable estate $16,500,000; tentative tax under §2001(c) of $6,545,800 less the applicable credit on the $15,000,000 basic exclusion ($5,945,800) → $600,000 of tax, 40% on the excess; the DSUE amount elected on Form 706 for the surviving spouse

Form 709 for 2026: a married couple gives $50,000 to each of three children with gift-splitting — two $19,000 annual exclusions per donee leave $12,000 taxable per child, $36,000 in all applied against the lifetime exclusion; a five-year §529 election on a $190,000 contribution; a $60,000 tuition payment made directly to the university excluded entirely under §2503(e)

GST: a $3,000,000 direct skip to a grandchild with exemption allocated on the return versus the 40% flat tax on an unallocated skip; a house transferred to a child while the parent keeps living in it rent-free pulled back under §2036 at date-of-death value, with the §1014 step-up that follows

Fiduciary income tax: a simple trust with $80,000 of dividends and $10,000 of capital gains allocated to corpus — DNI, the §651 distribution deduction, the beneficiary's Schedule K-1, the trust's own tax on the retained gains at the 2026 compressed brackets (Rev. Proc. 2025-32), and the grantor-trust rules of §§671–679 that make the whole computation vanish

connect_back.topic: Wealth management and the long horizon

sources: IRS Forms 706, 709 and 1041 and their instructions for the run year; Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (2026 basic exclusion amount and annual exclusion)
P.L. 119-21 §70106 (basic exclusion amount)
Bittker & Lokken, Federal Taxation of Income, Estates and Gifts (Thomson Reuters), transfer-tax chapters; Stephens, Maxfield, Lind & Calfee, Federal Estate and Gift Taxation (Thomson Reuters)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Tax procedure and the ethics of tax practice
days.headline_hint: A tax position is a bet with disclosed odds, and the Code prices every one of them
days.focus: The procedural Code and the rules of practice: statutes of limitation on assessment and refund (§§6501, 6511), the examination, appeals, deficiency and litigation paths (notice of deficiency, §6213 and the Tax Court, district court and the Court of Federal Claims, §7491 burden of proof, §7525 privilege), the penalty structure (§§6651, 6662, 6663, 6694, 6695, 6676, 6707A) with the standards of authority — reasonable basis, substantial authority, more likely than not — and disclosure on Form 8275; Circular 230 (31 CFR Part 10) duties and sanctions, the AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services as revised in 2024, §7216 confidentiality, and the limits of IRS authority over preparers. Professional-exam level: the reader can date every deadline on a timeline and price a position's penalty exposure.
parts: The clock: assessment, refund, extension and the events that stop it
From audit to court: examination, appeals, the ninety-day letter and choosing the forum
Penalties as prices: understatement, negligence, fraud, late filing — and who pays, taxpayer or preparer
Standards of authority: how sure you must be before you sign, and what disclosure buys
Circular 230 and the SSTSs: the duties a practitioner owes the client and the system
Confidentiality, privilege and the boundaries of the IRS's reach over preparers
worked_examples: A limitations timeline for a 2025 Form 1040 filed April 15, 2026: assessment barred after April 15, 2029 under §6501(a), six years if more than 25% of gross income was omitted (§6501(e)), no limit for fraud or no return; a refund claim under §6511 by the later of three years from filing or two years from payment; a notice of deficiency issued March 2028 and the 90-day Tax Court petition window under §6213 with the stay on assessment

Penalty arithmetic on a $60,000 understatement against $200,000 of correct tax: substantial understatement (greater of 10% of correct tax or $5,000) → 20% under §6662 = $12,000; if fraud, 75% under §6663; the preparer's §6694(a) penalty at the greater of $1,000 or 50% of the fee, §6694(b) at the greater of $5,000 or 75% for willful conduct; failure-to-file at 5% a month to 25% and failure-to-pay at 0.5% a month combined under §6651(c)

Standards applied to a real question: whether a $180,000 roof replacement is a deductible repair under §162 or a capitalized improvement under §263 and the tangible-property regulations (T.D. 9636) — reasonable basis with Form 8275 disclosure, substantial authority without it, more likely than not for a reportable transaction — and SSTS No. 1 (2024 revision) alongside Circular 230 §10.34

Circular 230 in practice: §10.21 on a client's discovered omission, §10.22 diligence, §10.27 contingent fees, §10.33 best practices, §10.36 firm procedures; the covered-opinion rules of the old §10.35 removed by T.D. 9668 (2014); Loving v. IRS, 742 F.3d 1013 (D.C. Cir. 2014) on the IRS's authority to license preparers; and a §7216 consent for disclosing return information
sources: Treasury Department Circular No. 230 (31 CFR Part 10, as amended by T.D. 9668, 2014; proposed revisions REG-116610-20, 2024)
AICPA Statements on Standards for Tax Services (revised, effective January 1, 2024)
Loving v. IRS, 742 F.3d 1013 (D.C. Cir. 2014); Saltzman & Book, IRS Practice and Procedure (Thomson Reuters)
days.exam_map: REG Area I – Ethics, Professional Responsibilities and Federal Tax Procedures (Circular 230, SSTS, penalties, statutes of limitation, audits and appeals)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Contracts, UCC Article 2 and agency
days.headline_hint: Every invoice on the ledger is a promise the law will enforce — on terms neither side fully read
days.focus: Common-law contract formation (offer, acceptance, consideration, the objective theory), defenses (capacity, fraud, duress, mistake, illegality), the statute of frauds and parol evidence, performance, breach and remedies (expectation, reliance, restitution, consequential damages and mitigation), third-party rights; UCC Article 2 for the sale of goods (merchants, firm offers, the battle of the forms under §2-207, risk of loss, perfect tender and cure, express and implied warranties and their disclaimer, buyer's and seller's remedies); and agency under the Restatement (Third) — actual and apparent authority, ratification, disclosed and undisclosed principals, respondeat superior and the agent's fiduciary duties. Professional-exam level with numbers in every remedy.
parts: A contract is what a reasonable person would think was agreed: formation and the objective theory
Defenses, writings and the words that never make it in: statute of frauds and parol evidence
Article 2 changes the rules for goods: merchants, firm offers and the battle of the forms
Delivery, risk of loss, perfect tender and the warranties that travel with the goods
Remedies with arithmetic: cover, market damages, lost volume and the Hadley limit
Agency: who can bind whom, and who pays when the agent causes harm
worked_examples: Battle of the forms under UCC §2-207: a purchase order for 5,000 aluminum extrusions with 30-day payment terms meets an acknowledgment adding an arbitration clause and a warranty disclaimer — which terms enter the contract between merchants under §2-207(2), and what §2-207(3) supplies when the forms never agreed, with Hill v. Gateway 2000 (7th Cir. 1997) on terms in the box

Remedies computed: the seller repudiates a $120,000 contract; the buyer covers at $135,000 (§2-712) or takes market damages at $131,000 (§2-713); a lost-volume dealer recovers lost profit under §2-708(2); consequential damages under §2-715 and Hadley v. Baxendale (1854) for a shut-down production line the seller was told about

Risk of loss and warranties: FOB shipping point versus FOB destination under §2-509, a nonconforming shipment shifting risk back under §2-510, the perfect-tender rule of §2-601 and the seller's right to cure under §2-508; §§2-313, 2-314 and 2-315 warranties tested against a real consumer limited warranty and its conspicuous §2-316 disclaimer

Agency on real fact patterns: a purchasing manager's actual authority versus the apparent authority a supplier relies on, ratification of an unauthorized order, an undisclosed principal's liability, respondeat superior for a delivery driver's accident versus an independent contractor's, and the agent's duty of loyalty — with Lucy v. Zehmer (Va. 1954) and Hamer v. Sidway (N.Y. 1891) anchoring formation and consideration
sources: Restatement (Second) of Contracts (1981); Farnsworth, Contracts (4th ed., Aspen)
Uniform Commercial Code Article 2 (Official Text), §§2-201, 2-205, 2-206, 2-207, 2-313 to 2-316, 2-508 to 2-510, 2-601, 2-703 to 2-715
Restatement (Third) of Agency (2006)
Hill v. Gateway 2000, Inc., 105 F.3d 1147 (7th Cir. 1997); Hadley v. Baxendale, 9 Ex. 341 (1854); Lucy v. Zehmer, 84 S.E.2d 516 (Va. 1954)

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Secured transactions, bankruptcy, business entities and fiduciary duties
days.headline_hint: When the money runs out, the law has already decided who stands where in line
days.focus: UCC Article 9 (attachment, perfection by filing, possession, control and automatic perfection, purchase-money security interests and their windows, priority rules, proceeds, buyers in ordinary course, default and disposition); the Bankruptcy Code (Chapters 7, 11 and 13 and Subchapter V, the automatic stay, the estate, executory contracts, priorities, preferences and fraudulent transfers, discharge and its exceptions, plan confirmation and absolute priority); suretyship; and business entities — formation and governance of corporations, LLCs and limited partnerships, the duties of care and loyalty, the business judgment rule, oversight liability, exculpation and veil-piercing — closing with the CPA's own civil liability. Professional-exam level, on a real Chapter 11 docket.
parts: Attachment, perfection and the race to the filing office
Priority: purchase-money interests, buyers in ordinary course, proceeds and what happens on default
Bankruptcy's architecture: the stay, the estate, the chapters and the priority ladder
Clawbacks and discharge: preferences, fraudulent transfers and the debts that survive
Entities and the people who run them: care, loyalty, the business judgment rule and oversight
The accountant's own exposure: privity, negligence, §11 and Rule 10b-5
worked_examples: An Article 9 priority timeline: a bank files a blanket financing statement on all equipment and inventory on January 10; a PMSI lender delivers a $400,000 machine on June 1 and files on June 15 (inside the 20-day window of §9-324(a)); an inventory PMSI that needed advance notice under §9-324(b); a buyer in ordinary course taking free under §9-320; proceeds under §9-315; and a commercially reasonable disposition under §§9-610 and 9-615 with the surplus and deficiency computed

Spirit Airlines' Chapter 11 (S.D.N.Y., petition November 18, 2024): the §362 automatic stay, §364 debtor-in-possession financing, the §507 priority ladder, the prepackaged plan confirmed under §1129 with equity cancelled under the absolute-priority rule, and the March 2025 emergence — contrasted with an individual's Chapter 7 (§§523 and 727 discharge exceptions) and Subchapter V's post-2024 debt ceiling

Clawbacks: a $250,000 payment to an unsecured supplier 60 days before the petition tested under §547(b), the ordinary-course and subsequent-new-value defenses of §547(c), the one-year insider window; a §548 constructive fraudulent transfer where an insolvent debtor sold an asset for less than reasonably equivalent value; a surety's rights of exoneration, reimbursement and subrogation

Fiduciary duties in Delaware: the business judgment rule and §102(b)(7) exculpation, Smith v. Van Gorkom (1985) on care, Caremark (1996) and Marchand v. Barnhill (2019) on oversight of mission-critical risk; an LLC operating agreement under RULLCA; veil-piercing factors; and the CPA's liability from Ultramares v. Touche (N.Y. 1931) to §11 of the Securities Act (no scienter) and Rule 10b-5 (scienter required)
sources: Uniform Commercial Code Article 9 (2010 amendments), §§9-203, 9-308 to 9-324, 9-609 to 9-625

Delaware General Corporation Law §§102(b)(7), 141, 144; Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (2006, amended 2013); Smith v. Van Gorkom, 488 A.2d 858 (Del. 1985); In re Caremark, 698 A.2d 959 (Del. Ch. 1996); Marchand v. Barnhill, 212 A.3d 805 (Del. 2019)
Ultramares Corp. v. Touche, 174 N.E. 441 (N.Y. 1931); Securities Act of 1933 §11; Exchange Act Rule 10b-5

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Financial statement analysis for decisions
days.headline_hint: Ratios are questions; the decision is what you do when two of them disagree
days.focus: Analysis aimed at a decision rather than a description: the five-step DuPont decomposition and what drives each term, cash-flow-based measures and accrual quality, credit analysis (coverage, leverage, the agency grids and distress scores), non-GAAP measures under Regulation G and Item 10(e), segment analysis after ASU 2023-07, earnings-per-share quality, common-size and trend analysis across cycles, and pro forma forecasting with the percent-of-sales method, external financing needed and sustainable growth. Practitioner level: the reader can take two real 10-Ks, say which business is better and why, and build the forecast that tests the claim.
parts: DuPont in five steps: where return on equity actually comes from
Cash against accruals: the measures that survive an aggressive accounting policy
Credit analysis: coverage, leverage, the rating grids and the scores that predict distress
Non-GAAP, segments and per-share numbers: reading around what management chose to show
Forecasting: percent of sales, financing needed, sustainable growth and the sensitivity that matters
worked_examples: Five-step DuPont on Costco's fiscal 2024 10-K (total revenue $254.5 billion, net income $7.37 billion) against Walmart's fiscal 2025 10-K (revenues $681.0 billion): tax burden, interest burden, operating margin, asset turnover and leverage — why Costco's return is built on turnover and Walmart's on margin and leverage, with every input taken from the filed statements

Credit analysis of Boeing's FY2024 10-K: interest coverage, debt to EBITDA and funds-from-operations to debt against the published rating-agency grid for aerospace and defense, an Altman Z''-score, and Spirit AeroSystems' FY2024 going-concern position (gross loss $1.37 billion) read through the same ratios

Non-GAAP and segments: Uber's FY2024 adjusted EBITDA reconciled to GAAP net income under Regulation G, Item 10(e) and the SEC staff's 2022 Compliance and Disclosure Interpretations 100.01–100.06; Amazon's FY2024 segment note under ASU 2023-07 with AWS operating income against the rest of the company

A pro forma forecast for a private manufacturer at 8% sales growth by the percent-of-sales method: the external financing needed, sustainable growth rate g = ROE × retention, a sensitivity table over growth and margin, and the Beneish M-score applied to Kraft Heinz's restated 2017–2018 periods
sources: Penman, Financial Statement Analysis and Security Valuation (5th ed., McGraw Hill); Subramanyam, Financial Statement Analysis (11th ed.)

CFA Institute, Financial Statement Analysis (2024 curriculum readings); Altman, 'Financial Ratios, Discriminant Analysis and the Prediction of Corporate Bankruptcy', Journal of Finance (1968); Beneish, 'The Detection of Earnings Manipulation', Financial Analysts Journal (1999)
SEC Regulation G and Regulation S-K Item 10(e); SEC Division of Corporation Finance, Non-GAAP Financial Measures C&DIs (updated December 2022); ASC 280 as amended by ASU 2023-07
Costco Wholesale Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal 2024; Walmart Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2025; The Boeing Company Form 10-K for fiscal 2024; Uber Technologies Form 10-K for fiscal 2024

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Cost accounting, budgets, variances and forecasting
days.headline_hint: A variance is the distance between the plan and the world, decomposed until someone owns each piece
days.focus: Managerial accounting as the exam and a plant manager both use it: cost behavior and estimation (high-low, regression), cost-volume-profit and operating leverage, absorption versus variable costing, job and process costing, activity-based costing and its death spiral, the master budget from sales to the cash budget, flexible budgets and the full standard-cost variance set (materials price and quantity, labor rate and efficiency, variable-overhead spending and efficiency, fixed-overhead budget and volume) reconciled to actual, transfer pricing, and prospective financial information under AT-C 305. Practitioner level: the reader can build the budget, compute every variance from real input prices and say which manager answers for each.
parts: Cost behavior: fixed, variable, mixed, and the regression that estimates them
Cost-volume-profit and operating leverage on a real income statement
Absorption, variable, job, process and activity-based costing: five answers to what a unit costs
The master budget: sales to production to purchases to cash
Standard costs and the variance tree, reconciled to the penny
Transfer prices, projections and the standards for numbers about the future
worked_examples: Standard-cost variances with real input prices: an aluminum window-frame maker's materials price variance computed from the LME aluminum cash-settlement monthly averages for two named 2025 months (the run pulls the figures), materials quantity, labor rate and efficiency, variable-overhead spending and efficiency, and fixed-overhead budget and volume variances, all reconciled from the static budget through the flexible budget to actual

Cost-volume-profit on Southwest Airlines' FY2024 operating statistics (RASM, CASM, available seat miles and load factor from the 10-K): the break-even load factor, degree of operating leverage, and what one cent of CASM does to operating income

Activity-based costing for two products sharing setups, inspections and machine hours: cost per unit under a single volume-based rate versus ABC, the over-costing of the simple product and the death spiral that follows; a transfer price at variable cost plus opportunity cost when the selling division is at capacity

A master budget for a seasonal retailer through the cash budget with collection lags and a line-of-credit draw; maintenance cost estimated by high-low versus ordinary least squares on 24 months of machine hours; and the AT-C 305 rules for a projection an outside party will see (assumptions, compilation versus examination)
sources: Datar & Rajan, Horngren's Cost Accounting: A Managerial Emphasis (17th ed., Pearson)
Kaplan & Cooper, Cost & Effect (Harvard Business School Press, 1998); Kaplan & Anderson, Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing (2007)
AICPA AT-C section 305 (Prospective Financial Information) and the AICPA Guide: Prospective Financial Information
Southwest Airlines Co. Form 10-K for fiscal 2024 (operating statistics); London Metal Exchange, aluminum cash-settlement monthly averages

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Derivatives and hedge accounting under ASC 815
days.headline_hint: Hedge accounting is permission to tell the truth about two instruments at once
days.focus: The definition of a derivative (underlying, notional, little or no initial net investment, net settlement) and its scope exceptions, embedded derivatives and the clearly-and-closely-related test, own-equity contracts under ASC 815-40 after ASU 2020-06, and the three hedge models — fair value, cash flow and net investment — with designation, documentation, effectiveness assessment, the shortcut and critical-terms-match methods, the ASU 2017-12 and ASU 2022-01 simplifications, discontinuation, and the ASC 815-10-50 disclosures; valuation of the instruments from the year-one derivatives lessons. Professional-exam level: the reader can decide whether an instrument is a derivative, choose the hedge model and post every entry through income and OCI.
parts: What makes an instrument a derivative, and the contracts the definition deliberately leaves out
Embedded derivatives and contracts on your own stock: the tests that decide where the value goes
Fair value hedges: the hedged item moves too, and the income statement shows both
Cash flow hedges: parking the gain in OCI until the forecasted transaction arrives
Net investment hedges, effectiveness, discontinuation and the disclosure table
worked_examples: Is it a derivative? ASC 815-10-15-83's four characteristics applied to a Southwest jet-fuel option, an Apple foreign-currency forward, a purchase order for 1,000 tons of hot-rolled coil (the normal-purchases-and-normal-sales exception), and a SPAC warrant under ASC 815-40 as reclassified after the SEC staff statement of April 12, 2021

A fair value hedge of fixed-rate debt: a receive-fixed/pay-floating swap on a $1 billion 3.85% note (Apple's FY2024 10-K describes interest-rate swaps hedging its term debt) — the hedged item's fair-value change on a 25-basis-point move computed with DV01 from day 50 of year one, the swap's offsetting change, the income-statement geography under ASU 2017-12 and the conditions for the shortcut method

Southwest's fuel hedges from its FY2024 10-K (WTI, Brent and heating-oil contracts; the $37 million second-half 2024 loss on undesignated WTI positions): AOCI deferral, reclassification as the fuel is consumed, the discontinuation when forecasted purchases cease to be probable, and the 2024 decision to add no new hedges through 2027

A euro-denominated borrowing designated as a net-investment hedge of a European subsidiary; a convertible note's conversion feature after ASU 2020-06; the clearly-and-closely-related test on an inflation-indexed lease; and the tabular ASC 815-10-50 disclosure of fair values by hedge type built from Apple's FY2024 derivatives note

days.subject: Accounting
days.topic: Data analytics in accounting and audit
days.headline_hint: The ledger is a dataset, and the auditor who can query it does not need to sample it
days.focus: Analytics as a working accountant and auditor use them: getting the data (XBRL and EDGAR's structured APIs, the AICPA Audit Data Standards, ETL and data quality), full-population tests in place of samples, journal-entry testing under AS 2401, Benford's law and digit analysis with proper thresholds, regression-based analytical procedures with prediction intervals as investigation thresholds, anomaly detection (isolation forests) and its leakage traps, process mining and continuous auditing, and where the human judgment still sits. The capstone: the reader rebuilds a company's analysis from tagged facts and runs the audit analytics himself. Practitioner level; closes with the forty-lesson course's prose statement of what a practitioner is expected to know.
parts: Where the numbers live: XBRL, EDGAR's APIs and the audit data standards
Testing everything instead of some things: full-population procedures and what they still cannot prove
Journal-entry testing and Benford's law: the classic screens, with their real false-positive rates
Regression as an analytical procedure: the expectation, the interval and the threshold
Anomaly detection and its traps: isolation forests, leakage and the analyst who fools himself
The capstone: rebuilding a 10-K from its tags and running the audit over it — and what a practitioner is expected to know
worked_examples: Pulling Apple's facts from EDGAR's companyfacts API (CIK 0000320193; data.sec.gov is on the terminal's allowlist) and rebuilding the FY2020–FY2024 ratio set and the day-17 DuPont decomposition from tagged us-gaap elements, then diffing against the filed 10-K — where custom extension tags and dimensional facts make the two disagree

Benford's law on the SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (the 2024q4 num.txt file): the first-digit distribution of every reported value against the Benford expectation (30.1% ones, 17.6% twos, down to 4.6% nines), the chi-square and mean-absolute-deviation tests with Nigrini's conformity thresholds, and why a single company's 10-K is too small a population to test

Journal-entry testing under AS 2401.58–.62 on a published sample general ledger (the AICPA Audit Data Standards sample data, or a disclosed synthetic ledger where none is public): entries posted on weekends, by senior management, in round amounts, to seldom-used accounts and near period-end; then an isolation forest (Liu, Ting & Zhou, 2008) over the same features, the two lists reconciled, and the day-89 leakage lesson applied to the features

A regression-based analytical procedure: expected monthly revenue from store count, trading days and a seasonal index over 36 months, the prediction interval as the AS 2305 / AU-C 520 investigation threshold, and the write-up of the two months that fall outside it — with the closing 'what a practitioner is expected to know' paragraph for the whole forty-lesson course
sources: AICPA, Guide to Audit Data Analytics (2017); AICPA Audit Data Standards (General Ledger and Subledger standards)
PCAOB AS 2401 ¶¶ .58–.67 (journal-entry testing) and AS 2305; AICPA AU-C 520
Nigrini, Benford's Law: Applications for Forensic Accounting, Auditing, and Fraud Detection (Wiley, 2012); Liu, Ting & Zhou, 'Isolation Forest', IEEE ICDM (2008)
SEC EDGAR XBRL APIs (companyfacts, frames) documentation; SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (quarterly); SEC Inline XBRL rules (Release 33-10514)

days.subject: Wealth Management
days.topic: The financial planning process and fiduciary standards
days.headline_hint: Whose side is the adviser on? Four legal answers to one question, and what each costs the client
days.focus: The seven-step planning process as CFP Board's Code and Standards defines it, mapped against the four legal standards that actually govern advice in the United States: the Investment Advisers Act §206 fiduciary duty as read in SEC v. Capital Gains Research Bureau, Regulation Best Interest for broker-dealers, ERISA §3(21) for plan advice after the 2024 Retirement Security Rule was vacated in March 2026, and the NAIC best-interest model for annuities. The reader learns the compensation models (AUM, flat, hourly, commission, fee-based versus fee-only), how to read a Form ADV Part 2A and a Form CRS, and the disclosure-versus-avoidance distinction in conflicts. Afterwards he can place any adviser on the standards map and price the difference in 30-year dollars.
parts: The seven steps are a liability map, not a checklist: what the Code and Standards actually requires at each one
Capital Gains Research Bureau and the fiduciary duty that Congress never wrote down
Regulation Best Interest: what 'best interest' means when it does not mean fiduciary
ERISA, the vacated 2024 rule and PTE 2020-02: who is a fiduciary to a rollover
Reading a Form ADV: fee schedules, conflicts and the thirty-year cost of a percentage point
Engagement letters, scope and the Hartwells' first meeting
worked_examples: SEC v. Capital Gains Research Bureau, 375 U.S. 180 (1963): the scalping facts and the holding that §206 imports a duty of disclosure of conflicts

A published Form ADV Part 2A fee schedule (Vanguard Personal Advisor's tiered AUM fee, as filed on IAPD) applied to the Hartwells' $400,000 portfolio: 30 years at 6% gross with a 1.00% fee ends at about $1.73 million and with 0.30% at about $2.11 million, so the fee gap is worth about $380,000

The DOL's Federal Register notice of court vacatur of the Retirement Security Rule (March 20, 2026) and the restored text of PTE 2020-02: which of the Hartwells' rollover conversations are fiduciary advice and which are not
A Form CRS read line by line against Reg BI's four obligations (disclosure, care, conflict of interest, compliance) for a hypothetical dual-registrant recommending a variable annuity

DOL, Retirement Security Rule: Notice of Court Vacatur, 91 Fed. Reg. (March 20, 2026); PTE 2020-02 as originally published December 18, 2020

days.subject: Wealth Management
days.topic: Client psychology and behavioural finance in practice
days.headline_hint: The 1.2 points a year that investors pay for their own behaviour, and what a planner can do about it on a Tuesday
days.focus: Year one's day 140 established that the rational-agent model fails; this lesson is the practice that follows. It measures the behaviour gap with Morningstar's Mind the Gap 2025, separates risk tolerance (psychometric), risk capacity (arithmetic) and risk need (goal-based), teaches the Klontz money-script framework and the Grable-Lytton scale as instruments rather than slogans, and works through the counselling and communication methods CFP Board added as Domain H in 2021. The reader can afterwards run a discovery meeting, score a risk questionnaire, translate a client's stated goals into a goals-based allocation, and design the default and commitment devices that Save More Tomorrow proved.
parts: Mind the Gap: how a fund can return 8.2% while its investors earn 7.0%
Tolerance, capacity and need are three different numbers, and only one of them is a feeling
Money scripts and the discovery meeting: turning Klontz's four categories into questions
Save More Tomorrow and the architecture of defaults: what the 2004 field study actually measured
Goals-based planning: Chhabra's three buckets and the mental accounting that helps rather than hurts
March 2020 as a case file: the sell-at-the-bottom arithmetic and the conversation that prevents it
worked_examples: Morningstar, Mind the Gap 2025: the 1.2-percentage-point annual gap between investor returns (7.0%) and total returns (8.2%) over 2015-2024, applied to the Hartwells' $400,000 for ten years, about $45,000 of foregone terminal wealth

Thaler and Benartzi (2004): participants who accepted Save More Tomorrow raised their average saving rate from 3.5% to 13.6% over four raises, and the Hartwells' equivalent commitment device on Dana's annual merit increase

The S&P 500 from 3,386.15 (February 19, 2020) to 2,237.40 (March 23, 2020) and back above 3,200 by June 8, 2020: the dollar cost to a $400,000 portfolio of selling at the close on March 23 and re-entering on June 8, using the index closes

Scoring the 13-item Grable-Lytton risk-tolerance scale for Dana and Marcus separately, then confronting the score with the household's risk capacity computed as the maximum drawdown the 2034 college goal can absorb
sources: Morningstar, Mind the Gap 2025 (the U.S. investor-return study, 2015-2024 window)
Thaler, R. and Benartzi, S., 'Save More Tomorrow: Using Behavioral Economics to Increase Employee Saving', Journal of Political Economy 112(S1), 2004

Klontz, B., Britt, S., Mentzer, J. and Klontz, T., 'Money Beliefs and Financial Behaviors: Development of the Klontz Money Script Inventory', Journal of Financial Therapy 2(1), 2011; Grable, J. and Lytton, R., 'Financial risk tolerance revisited', Financial Services Review 8, 1999

Chhabra, A., 'Beyond Markowitz: A Comprehensive Wealth Allocation Framework for Individual Investors', Journal of Wealth Management 7(4), 2005; CFP Board, The Psychology of Financial Planning (2021 Principal Knowledge Domain H)

days.subject: Wealth Management
days.topic: Cash-flow and debt management
days.headline_hint: A household is a small company with a bad chart of accounts: the statements, the ratios and the arithmetic of every loan the Hartwells carry
days.focus: Personal financial statements built to the same discipline as year one's corporate ones, the planning ratios that lenders and planners actually use (28/36 housing, the 43% and 50% DTI limits in the agency underwriting guides, savings rate, liquidity), and the mechanics of household debt done to the bottom: fixed-rate amortization, the refinancing NPV, credit-card minimum-payment dynamics at the Fed's G.19 average APR, HELOCs, auto loans and the federal student-loan system as rewritten by the 2025 reconciliation law (the Repayment Assistance Plan from July 1, 2026). The reader can afterwards build the Hartwells' balance sheet and cash-flow statement, rank their debts by after-tax cost, and decide pay-down versus invest with a number.
parts: The household balance sheet and cash-flow statement: what to mark to market and what to leave at cost
Ratios that mean something: housing, total debt service, savings rate and the lender's DTI
Amortization from first principles: the payment formula, the balance formula and where the interest goes
Refinancing is a capital-budgeting decision: closing costs, break-even and the NPV over the horizon you will actually keep the loan
Revolving credit and the minimum-payment trap; avalanche versus snowball as arithmetic and as psychology
Student loans after the 2025 law: standard, RAP and the deduction the Hartwells have already lost
worked_examples: The Hartwells' $372,000 30-year mortgage at 6.625% (originated 2023): payment $2,381.96, balance $358,968 after 36 payments, about $23,600 of interest in year four, and the pay-down-versus-invest comparison at their combined marginal rate

Refinancing that balance to 5.75% for the remaining 27 years with $6,500 of closing costs: payment $2,184.21, monthly saving $197.75, break-even 33 months, and a five-year NPV of about +$4,200 at a 4% discount rate; then the same numbers at the Freddie Mac PMMS rate on the run date

An $8,000 balance at the Fed G.19 average APR on accounts assessed interest (about 22% in 2025): the payoff time and total interest under the issuer's minimum-payment formula versus a fixed $300 a month, and why the 2%-of-balance minimum never finishes

Dana's $28,000 of Direct loans at 5.50%: the 10-year standard payment versus the Repayment Assistance Plan's 1%-10%-of-AGI schedule less $50 per dependent, and the §221 interest deduction the household loses above the 2026 $175,000-$205,000 MFJ phase-out
sources: Dalton, M. and Dalton, J., Fundamentals of Financial Planning, 9th ed. (Money Education), the personal financial statements and ratio chapters
IRS Publication 936, Home Mortgage Interest Deduction (the $750,000 acquisition-debt limit made permanent by P.L. 119-21); IRC §163(h), §221
Congressional Research Service, 'The Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP) in P.L. 119-21' (IF13075); Federal Reserve Statistical Release G.19, Consumer Credit
Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey; Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-6 (debt-to-income ratios)

days.subject: Wealth Management
days.topic: Emergency reserves and liquidity
days.headline_hint: Cash is an insurance policy with a visible premium: sizing the reserve, choosing where it sits, and pricing what it costs to hold
days.focus: The reserve as a self-insurance layer: how many months, of what expenses, for which household (two earners, one of them self-employed), and the liquidity ladder behind it, from Roth contribution basis and a HELOC to the SECURE 2.0 emergency provisions (the $1,000 penalty-free distribution, pension-linked emergency savings accounts up to $2,500, 401(k) loans under §72(p)). The vehicles are compared on after-tax yield with Pennsylvania's exemption of Treasury interest, and the opportunity cost of holding the reserve is priced as a present value against the cost of a forced sale in a drawdown. The reader can afterwards size and place the Hartwells' reserve and defend both numbers.
parts: What the reserve insures against, and why 'three to six months' is a range and not an answer
Bills, savings accounts, money funds and I bonds: after-tax yield when your state does not tax Treasuries
The liquidity ladder: Roth basis, HELOCs, plan loans and the SECURE 2.0 emergency provisions
The premium you pay to hold cash: a present-value calculation, and the drawdown that justifies it
The Fed's $400 question: what the SHED survey says about who has a reserve at all

Tax-equivalent yields at the 24% federal bracket plus Pennsylvania's 3.07%: a 13-week Treasury bill at the auction yield on the run date versus a high-yield savings account and a prime money-market fund, showing when the state exemption makes the bill win

The opportunity cost of a $70,000 reserve earning 4% instead of a 60/40 portfolio's expected 6.5% over 30 years, discounted to a present value, set against the realised 2022 60/40 drawdown of about 16% and the tax cost of a forced sale
Roth IRA ordering under §408A(d)(4): the Hartwells' $60,000 of Roth balances contain $46,000 of contribution basis that can be withdrawn tax- and penalty-free, and how that changes the reserve size

IRC §72(t)(2)(I) (emergency personal expense distributions) and §402A(e) (pension-linked emergency savings accounts), as added by SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022 §§115 and 127; IRC §72(p) plan loans; §408A(d)(4) Roth ordering rules
TreasuryDirect, Series I savings bond composite rate announcements; Treasury auction results for 13-week bills

days.subject: Wealth Management
days.topic: Education planning I: the savings vehicles
days.headline_hint: Eight years to a tuition bill that grows faster than wages: 529s, Coverdells, custodial accounts and the new §530A accounts, priced against each other
days.focus: The education funding problem as a present-value problem (the four-year cost stream grown at tuition inflation, discounted, and converted to a level contribution), then the vehicles at statute depth: §529 qualified expenses after the 2025 law (K-12 raised to $20,000, tutoring and credentialing added), the five-year gift election, the $35,000 lifetime 529-to-Roth rollover, the 10% penalty and its exceptions, Pennsylvania's per-beneficiary deduction tied to the gift exclusion, Coverdell ESAs, UTMA accounts under the kiddie tax, and the §530A accounts created in 2025. The reader can afterwards compute the Hartwells' required monthly contribution for two children and choose the account for each dollar.

§529 at statute depth: qualified expenses, the 2025 expansions, penalties and the Roth rollover escape hatch
Pennsylvania's deduction, the five-year election and the gift-tax mechanics of front-loading

The §530A account: what the 2025 law created, who gets the $1,000, and where it fits
One dollar, four homes: the after-tax growth of $10,000 in each vehicle over eleven years

The five-year election under §529(c)(2)(B): $95,000 per donor per beneficiary in 2026, the Form 709 reporting, and what happens to the exclusion if the donor dies in year three

days.subject: Wealth Management
days.topic: Education planning II: financial aid formulas and education tax benefits
days.headline_hint: The Student Aid Index is a means test with a marginal rate of 47%: how the formula treats income and assets, and what a planner can legally move
days.focus: The federal need-analysis formula after the FAFSA Simplification Act, worked from the Department of Education's published 2026-27 tables: income protection allowances, the 22%-47% assessment of adjusted available income, the 12% asset conversion (asset protection allowance now zero), the 20% student-asset rate, the treatment of 529s, custodial accounts and grandparent money, and the CSS Profile's institutional methodology alongside it. Then the tax side: the American Opportunity and Lifetime Learning credits, their unindexed phase-outs, the no-double-benefit rule with 529 distributions, and the federal loan limits and Parent PLUS caps that took effect July 1, 2026. The reader can afterwards compute a household's SAI, read its implicit marginal rates, and coordinate 529 withdrawals with the credits.

The parent formula worked: allowances, the assessment brackets and the 47% top rate
Assets are taxed at 5.64% or 20% depending on whose name is on them
The Profile schools: home equity, sibling assets and the institutional methodology
The credits: AOTC and LLC mechanics, the phase-outs that were never indexed, and the 529 coordination rule
Loans after July 2026: Direct limits, Parent PLUS caps and what fills the gap

days.subject: Wealth Management
days.topic: Life insurance needs analysis
days.headline_hint: How much is a life worth to the people who depend on it? Three methods, one household, and the present values that separate them
days.focus: The three needs-analysis methods taught to the bottom: human life value (Huebner's 1927 framing as a growing annuity net of self-consumption), the needs approach (immediate cash needs, dependency-period income, lifetime income for the survivor, education, less resources), and capital retention versus capital liquidation. Resources are priced honestly: Social Security survivor benefits from the PIA bend points and the family maximum, the earnings test, group term through §79 with the Table I imputed income, and existing assets. The reader can afterwards produce a defensible face amount for each Hartwell spouse, show the sensitivity to the discount rate, and explain why the two methods disagree by a million dollars.
parts: Huebner's human life value: earnings, growth, self-consumption and the discount rate that swings the answer
The needs approach: cash needs at death, the dependency period, the survivor's lifetime and the education fund
Survivor benefits are a real asset: PIA bend points, the 75% child and parent benefits, the family maximum and the earnings test
Capital retention versus capital liquidation: the same income need, two very different lump sums
Group term is not free: §79, Table I and the imputed income on Dana's two-times-salary policy
Two spouses, two answers: the Hartwells' face amounts and how often to redo them

The needs approach for Dana: mortgage payoff $358,968, final expenses $15,000, the education fund PV from day 5, 15 years of $80,000 replacement income until Theo is 22, less survivor benefits computed from Dana's PIA at the run year's SSA bend points and the family maximum, less $400,000 of assets
Capital retention at a 3.5% real yield on an $80,000 income need is $2.29 million; capital liquidation over 27 years is $1.38 million; which the Hartwells should buy and why

Dana's employer-paid group term of two times salary ($296,000): the $246,000 above the §79 exclusion at the Table I rate for age 35-39 ($0.09 per $1,000 per month) produces $265.68 of imputed income a year, and the comparison with the cost of an individual 20-year level term policy
